Federal judge strikes down Trump administration's visa ban on 75 countries. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries met privately with Jared Kushner. Israel strikes Syria near the Golan Heights. U.S. envoy suggests Israel bombed Syria's Abu al-Duhur airbase to "bait" Turkey. Ukraine strikes Russian refinery, Russians strike Ukrainian mall. Sudanese Army strikes inside Chad. Venezuela unable to ship oil, Reuters reports. Embattled Mexican governor Ruben Rocha out again. Germany records over 14,000 heat-related deaths. DR Congo and M23 rebels agree on peace roadmap in Switzerland. Video shows hundreds held captive after mass abduction from Nigerian mosque. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, two Palestinians were killed and 32 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,422 killed, with 174,401 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,288 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,290, while 813 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israeli strikes kill six Palestinians on Monday: At least six Palestinians, including a child, were killed in Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip on Monday, Al Jazeera reported. A Palestinian was killed and others wounded when Israeli forces a tent sheltering displaced people near Al-Aqsa Martyrs hospital in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza, WAFA reported. Separately, another Palestinian died from wounds sustained in an Israeli airstrike on the Gaza City port area last Tuesday which killed seven. Israeli forces targeted a mosque and a water desalination plant in Gaza City's Sheikh Radwan district. Israel continues to kill in Gaza over the weekend despite "ceasefire": An Israeli drone struck a home in the Al-Bassa area north of Deir al-Balah on Saturday, killing one Palestinian man and wounding another. Separately, a woman was shot by Israeli forces near Nuseirat. Israeli artillery areas around Al-Bureij, Khan Younis, and eastern Gaza City on Saturday, including homes in Khan Younis' Al-Amal neighborhood. On Sunday, Israeli forces a Palestinian in Al-Maghazi refugee camp in central Gaza. In a separate airstrike near Al-Zawayda, Israel a 4-year-old Palestinian, sources told Drop Site, wounding two others Palestinian in the same strike. Israeli tanks also toward displacement tents near Asdaa City and Hamad Towers, warships opened fire off Rafah, and artillery shelling was reported in northern Al-Bureij on Sunday. Palestinian man executed by Israel in Gaza, family says: The family of Ibrahim Mohammed Kawarea Israeli forces executed the father of three after detaining him near the "Yellow Line" east of Khan Younis on Friday, according to Felesteen. Kawarea was suffering a severe mental health crisis. Relatives said his state of mind had worsened after his cousin had been killed days earlier. His uncle, Jaber Kawarea, said Ibrahim's body arrived at Nasser Medical Complex with multiple gunshot wounds to his head, chest, and abdomen--some apparently fired at close range--and his legs were still bound. "We were shocked that his legs were also tied," he said. The family described his killing as a "field execution" and is demanding an international investigation. Israeli forces kill Palestinian child, settler assaults elderly amputee as attacks continue across the West Bank: Nablus : Israeli forces shot and a 14-year-old Palestinian during a raid on New Askar refugee camp, east of Nablus, on Sunday. Israeli forces also continued their siege of three Palestinian homes in Qusra for the third consecutive week on Sunday, restricting movement and blocking aid and solidarity groups, while allowing settlers to move freely around the besieged homes. Israeli attackers on Sunday from one of these homes after occupying it for 10 days, but remained stationed outside the property. Hebron: An Israeli settler an elderly Palestinian amputee in Masafer Yatta on Saturday, while another videotaped it. After Saturday's assault, Israeli forces raided his home, confiscating his family's phones, per WAFA. Israel police announced on Sunday that two Israeli teenagers were arrested--the 16-year-old who clubbed the disabled Palestinian man and the 17-year-old who filmed the attack, to the Times of Israel. The 17-year-old was later released to house arrest, the police said. Jordan Valley: An Israeli settler was Sunday morning near the Palestinian village of Al-Auja in the occupied Jordan Valley, according to The New Arab. The 24-year-old man was being treated for his injuries as Israeli forces searched the area for the attacker. Al-Auja has been subjected to so much sustained settler violence that residents were forced to abandon the village earlier this year. Katz says Israeli military will act "forcefully" over kites from Gaza: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz the Israeli military on Sunday to "act immediately and forcefully" over kites launched from Gaza, declaring that Israel will treat every kite or balloon as an "act of war," even those carrying no explosives. Four kites flown from Gaza landed in Kibbutz Nahal Oz over the weekend, according to the Times of Israel. The Israeli military said nothing suspicious was found on them and they posed no danger to the public. "A balloon is treated like a kite, and a kite is treated like a drone, with or without explosives," Katz said, threatening those behind the launches with the "utmost severity." Senior Hamas official Basem Naim on Sunday, writing that it was a "surreal paradox" that a "nuclear state that practices terrorism daily" would "issue orders to deal forcefully with paper kites coming out of Gaza." Mohamed Awad to be detained without charge for months: Palestinian journalist and Drop Site contributor Mohamed Awad was to be held in administrative detention for four months by Israeli military authorities, according to his lawyer. Awad was arrested from his home in the village of Beitunia, near Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, on August 12 by the Israeli military. Administrative detention is a mechanism by which Israeli authorities imprison Palestinians indefinitely without charge or trial. Hamas tells Kushner that it will not abide by an unenforced deal: Senior Hamas official Osama Hamdan the group told Jared Kushner in their meeting last weekend that if Israel does not publicly accept the proposed framework and begin implementing its obligations, including halting attacks and withdrawing from Gaza, Hamas will not consider itself obligated to implement any part of the deal. Hamdan made the remarks on an Iraqi podcast released this week. Hamdan stressed that Hamas has not agreed to surrender its weapons. He said the framework calls for heavy weapons to be restricted and stored under the authority of a Palestinian administrative committee governing Gaza, while remaining in Palestinian hands. He also said that none of Hamas's weapons would be transferred to any non-Palestinian party and not a single bullet would leave Gaza under the agreement. Hamas discusses electoral strategy: Hamas said in a statement that it would the upcoming Palestinian legislative elections as part of the "broadest possible national alliance" to build a more unified Palestinian political system. Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas issued a decree on July 9 setting legislative elections for November 28 in Jerusalem, the West Bank, and Gaza. They would be the first Palestinian legislative elections since 2006. Hamas urged Abbas not to reverse course "as happened in previous stages." " Anti-Netanyahu" says there will be no Palestinian state if he controls government: Gadi Eisenkot, the former Israeli military chief of staff now leading in polls to unseat Benjamin Netanyahu in the October 27 election, on Saturday there will be no Palestinian state under a government he forms. "There is no Palestinian state, and in the government we will form, no Palestinian state will arise," he wrote on X. A recent New Yorker profile by editor David Remnick cast him as the "anti-Bibi" in "manner and character," a humble soldier fighting for a "Jewish, democratic, progressive, and liberal state." Iran U.S. to announce "economic D-Day" sanctions against Iran: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is set to announce new U.S. sanctions against Iran at a press conference on Monday afternoon. In an in the Financial Times, Bessent wrote: "At dawn begins an economic D-Day--the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary. Our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains the tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone." He added that any country that "serves as a financial artery" for Iran "should expect to share in its isolation" and would become a "global pariah." Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei criticized the move as "a clear example of economic terrorism to punish a nation that insists on defending its sovereignty and independence." He warned that Iran would respond harshly to expanded U.S. sanctions. "Any escalation of this situation will undoubtedly bring about consequences," Baghaei said. "Our hands are not tied." Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, other countries not to join the campaign against Iran, saying that "any country participating in the imposition of economic restrictions against us is considered an enemy." Rezaei said Iran is prepared to target "all American oil and economic companies in the region" if Washington escalates to economic war, and that in a full economic war, Iran would let no oil leave the Persian Gulf "even through other means," signaling potential strikes on bypasses. Iran permits Iraqi tankers to pass through Hormuz: Iran special permission for a number of Iraqi oil tankers to pass through the Strait of Hormuz after repeated requests from Baghdad, IRNA reported. The issue was a key request during Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf's visit to Iraq. The Iraqi President said Iran had already allowed the passage of vessels carrying Iraqi crude in recent days, according to Reuters. Iraq produced about 4 million barrels per day before the Iran war, and virtually all seaborne exports left from the southern Basra terminals in the Persian Gulf, meaning they had to pass through the Strait of Hormuz. Qatari spending dramatically reduced by war: Qatar is spending at home and abroad as the six-month U.S.-Israel war with Iran takes a severe toll on one of the world's richest states, the Financial Times reported. Qatari government departments have had budgets reduced by as much as 30%, according to the FT, while funding for overseas aid has been cut by about 85%. Qatar has also halted Liquified Natural Gas production, its main source of export revenue, after Iranian strikes damaged the Ras Laffan complex and the war disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The International Monetary Fund expects Qatar's economy to contract 8.6% this year, the steepest decline among the six Gulf states. Qatar is leaning on its roughly $500 billion sovereign wealth fund to absorb the shock from the war, but officials are reportedly considering deeper cuts if the crisis continues. U.S. officials claim that 40 tankers crossed Hormuz on Friday; data shows none: Three U.S. officials Axios's Barak Ravid on Saturday that 40 tankers crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, carrying 16 million barrels of oil out of the Gulf. Kpler's vessel-tracking data, however, showed zero west-to-east tanker crossings on Friday and zero barrels of oil exiting through the Strait. Iranian refinery approaching full repair, official says: The repair of Iran's South Pars Phase 14 gas refinery, in an Israeli strike during the 12-day war in June 2025, is 70% complete, Pars Oil and Gas Company CEO Touraj Dehqani said on Saturday, according to Iran's oil ministry news agency SHANA. Dehqani claimed the refinery would be fully restored and its damaged section reintegrated into the production cycle by year's end. South Pars, the offshore field Iran shares with Qatar in the Persian Gulf, is the world's largest gas field and supplies roughly 80% of Iran's natural gas. Iran's oil minister also the discovery of more than 7.5 trillion cubic feet of natural gas in southern Fars province on Sunday. Pakistan army chief set to visit Iran on Monday: Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir arrived in Tehran on Monday, according to Iran's Tasnim news agency. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said the trip is part of Pakistan's continuing efforts to strengthen "peace and security" in the region, per New Arab. Al Jazeera's Ali Hashem says the meeting is meant to reactivate mediation between the U.S. and Iran. Iran announces it will choke "shuttle" trade through Hormuz: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority on Sunday that any vessel cooperating with a blacklisted ship, including through ship-to-ship (STS) transfers, will be blacklisted and face fines, detention, or confiscation on future Strait of Hormuz passages. The move seeks to thwart the workaround that has kept oil moving despite Iran's grip on the strait: a "shuttle" trade in which tankers make short, dark-transit runs through Hormuz with transponders off, then transfer their cargo to other ships via STS just outside the Gulf. Energy analysts have said this covert corridor is a major reason global supply hasn't collapsed. U.S. authorities say it is helping move about 8 million barrels daily. Yemen Ansarallah targets Saudi oil tanker in the Red Sea: The group's military spokesperson issued a saying an oil tanker belonging to Saudi Arabia "was targeted off the coast of Yanbu in Saudi Arabia with a ballistic missile." Earlier in the day, the UK Maritime Trade Operations said a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile about 63 nautical miles west of Yanbu, Saudi Arabia, causing a fire on the vessel's main deck. Lebanon Israeli forces kill two 17-year-old boys, demolish and burn homes across Southern Lebanon despite ceasefire: In Mays Al-Jabal in the Marjayoun district, Israeli bulldozers a temporary school complex in the Dbayeh area, while troops brought in explosives and rigged several homes for demolition, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. In Khiam, forces homes near Al-Mabarrat schools before setting fire to additional homes, properties and agricultural fields. The bodies of two 17-year-old boys who had been missing since Sunday were from the Dawhat Kfar Remman area in Nabatieh. Lebanon's Health Ministry said they had been killed in an Israeli attack with reports saying an Israeli drone struck the motorcycle they were riding. On Saturday, Israeli warplanes struck Ali Al-Taher hill twice, and Israeli artillery hit Dawhat Kfar Remman, Dabsha hill and the wooded area around Ali Al-Taher with phosphorus shells, according to NNA. Two additional Israeli airstrikes hit between Sirbin and Rshaf. No injuries were reported in that strike. Israeli troops demolished civilian homes in the Zawtar pilot zone; reporting from journalist Courtney Bonneau. U.S. envoy walks back comments on Hezbollah role in negotiations: U.S. envoy Tom Barrack walked back remarks suggesting Hezbollah and Iran should be represented in negotiations surrounding Lebanon. In an interview with Mario Nawfal on Saturday, Barrack that any serious settlement in Lebanon requires Hezbollah and Iran at the negotiating table and the U.S. negotiating team is trying to bring them into the process. "The problem is you don't have the people who can make decisions at the table," Barrack told Mario Nawfal. "The people who can make the decision are Hezbollah and Iran." On Sunday, however, Barrack told the Associated Press that he had been describing the difficulty of resolving Hezbollah's weapons rather than proposing their participation in negotiations. "Hezbollah is a designated foreign terrorist organization. We do not negotiate with it, and nothing I said suggests otherwise," he said. U.S. News Thousands are still without power in northwest Indiana after deadly storms, sparking lawsuit : More than 28,000 customers without power as of Sunday in northwest Indiana following storms that began August 11, which killed at least seven people and displaced about 1,000. In Gary, a majority-Black city where more than half of residents lost power and about one in three lives in poverty, resident Shatiya Hardin described conditions as "absolutely horrible," saying that families are struggling with the heat and that many rely on a community center for meals, air conditioning, and phone charging. Indiana Gov. Mike Braun requested an expedited major disaster declaration from FEMA for 54 counties, estimating losses could exceed $5 billion. Father of USS Abraham Lincoln sailor detained by ICE while son deployed at sea: Luis Manuel Aviles , a Nicaraguan immigrant who has lived in the U.S. for roughly 20 years, was by Border Patrol during a traffic stop in Key West, Florida, on Saturday, his family said. His son Joshua Aviles serves aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, which has been deployed at sea for more than nine months. Family members said Aviles had a work permit, Social Security card, and driver's license. There have been more than 50 documented detentions of parents and spouses of active-duty service members during Trump's second term, according to a recent Associated Press investigation. Canada "at war" over trade after U.S.-Canada talks collapse, oil supply squeeze looming for U.S. refiners: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney Canada "at war" over trade after suspending talks with the U.S., saying President Donald Trump "miscalculated" by demanding a "bad deal" that included new restrictions on Canada's ability to strike trade agreements with other nations and "exclusive access" to Canadian critical minerals. The breakdown triggers new tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian exports on top of existing levies on steel, aluminum, lumber, and vehicles, with Carney saying Canada would match the fresh U.S. tariffs "dollar for dollar." Separately, U.S. refiners, which are processing the most crude oil in eight years and taking advantage of record diesel margins, face a supply drop from Canada, their largest foreign crude supplier, as planned maintenance in Alberta's oil sands is set to take about 300,000 barrels a day offline next month, according to reporting from Bloomberg. USPS moves forward with mail-in ballot restrictions: The U.S. Postal Service Friday new eligibility guidelines for mail-in ballots that closely mirror President Donald Trump's March executive order restricting the practice, according to The Hill, even though a federal judge later struck down that order. The 95-page report, set for official release August 26, would give states 60 days before the November 3 midterms to notify USPS if they intend to submit citizenship-based voter eligibility lists, echoing Trump's earlier order to the agency. U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani blocked the order's enforcement earlier this month, warning it would create "confusion" and "chaos" close to the election. Nearly a third of 2024 general election ballots were cast by mail, according to a U.S. Election Assistance Commission report. Trump made more than 1,000 stock trades in June, disclosure shows: President Donald Trump more than 1,000 securities trades in June, including significant purchases of Berkshire Hathaway, Visa, Mastercard, and Cintas, totaling between $78.1 million and $263.1 million, according to a financial disclosure published Saturday by the U.S. Office of Government Ethics. Trump made more than 21,000 securities trades worth between $600 million and $1.86 billion in 2025, often in bursts tied to market-moving events and occasionally involving same-day buying and selling of the same security. Migrants who resisted deportation flight to Liberia forced onward to Equatorial Guinea : At least five migrants who to get off a U.S. deportation flight in Liberia were instead flown to Equatorial Guinea on Thursday, the New York Times reported. Three of the deportees, all Cuban men, told the Times that officers placed knees on their necks while restraining them in Liberia, that they were told they would be returned to the U.S., and that instead they landed in Equatorial Guinea, where they were met by dozens of masked, armed officers and taken to a guarded hotel in the country's capital, Malabo. The case is part of a broader deal in which the U.S. approved a $5 million payment to Liberia to accept up to 1,200 deportees. Federal judge strikes down Trump administration 's visa ban on 75 countries: Judge Jeannette A. Vargas of the Southern District of New York Friday that the Trump administration's ban on issuing visas to immigrants from 75 countries was "contrary to law" and exceeded Secretary of State Marco Rubio 's legal authority, disputing the administration's stated rationale that targeted immigrants were likely to become "a financial burden to Americans." Vargas distinguished the case from the Supreme Court's 2018 upholding of Trump's first-term travel ban, noting that ruling concerned entry restrictions rather than visa issuance. The Trump administration is expected to appeal the decision. Jeffries met privately with Kushner amid preparations for possible Democratic House majority: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries privately in recent weeks in New York City with Jared Kushner , President Trump's top outside adviser and son-in-law, to discuss potential areas of common ground including housing, immigration, and cost of living, The New York Times reported on Saturday. Kushner suggested Jeffries meet with White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles , and has reportedly told others that Jeffries is "the most serious person among Democratic leaders" for any bipartisan dealmaking. The meeting comes as Trump's inner circle prepares for a possible Democratic House majority, with Jeffries telling the Times last month he has "not ruled anything in and not ruled anything out in terms of accountability," naming War Secretary Pete Hegseth as a cabinet official he wants "next on the list" for removal. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Israel strikes Syria near the Golan Heights: Israel a drone strike Saturday on a vehicle in Beit Jinn, southwest of Damascus near the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights. The Israeli military said it targeted a man it accused of being in the "final stages" of preparing an imminent attack on Israeli soldiers. Syrian state media said at least one person was wounded and condemned the strike as a violation of Syrian sovereignty. The attack came four days after Israel carried out a larger unprovoked aerial bombardment of the Abu al-Duhur airbase in Syria's northwestern Idlib province on August 18. Barrack suggests Israel bombed Syria 's Abu al-Duhur airbase to "bait" Turkey: U.S. envoy Tom Barrack U.S. intelligence found no Turkish military assets at the base and no plan by Ankara to move in, contradicting Netanyahu's justification for Tuesday's attack--and said Turkey was exercising "restraint." He warned Turkey could have scrambled fighter jets against the Israeli aircraft, potentially triggering "World War III." Barrack said another possibility was a "miscommunication" between Netanyahu's office, the Israeli military and Mossad. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz issued a rare Sabbath statement rejecting Barrack's account as "full of inaccuracies." Katz claimed Syria was warned directly, and said Washington was informed beforehand, something Barrack denied. Ukraine strikes Russian refinery, Russians strike Ukrainian mall: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Saturday that Ukrainian forces had struck Russia's Novokuybyshevsk oil refinery, roughly 1,000 kilometers from the front line, as Kyiv expands its long-range campaign against Russian energy and military infrastructure. Ukrainian forces also hit a logistics hub in the Samara region and targets in the Black Sea, according to Zelenskyy. Separately, Russian drones struck a busy shopping mall in Kryvyi Rih on Friday evening, killing at least 16 people and injuring more than 130, including 23 children, the Financial Times reports. As of Saturday morning, nine people remained missing, including two children. Twenty-nine victims were in serious condition, among them five children. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy the drones hit in two waves, with the second strike coming about 30 minutes later as emergency crews responded, a "double-tap" attack. Sudanese Army strikes inside of Chad: The Chadian military on Saturday that the Sudanese Army conducted a strike on vehicles roughly 100 kilometers into its territory, with reports suggesting the army targeted an RSF convoy traveling through the country. Previous reporting has documented similar convoys carrying arms shipments from the UAE through Chad. Venezuela unable to ship oil, Reuters reports: Venezuela's aging ports have it from moving crude oil as quickly as the country is producing and selling it, according to a Reuters report, with tankers waiting up to 30 days to load because of equipment failures, power outages, storage shortages, and crude-quality problems. Venezuela has been unable to push exports above roughly 1.25 million barrels per day, despite rising production and strong demand. Embattled Mexican governor Rocha out again: Sinaloa Gov. Ruben Rocha Moya is again, just a day after returning from leave, following intense pressure from his own party and President Claudia Sheinbaum. Rocha stepped away from office after being accused of drug trafficking and alleged collusion with the Sinaloa Cartel's Chapitos faction by U.S. authorities; he suddenly announced Friday he would return only to then reverse course Saturday, saying he would take an indefinite leave. Morena leaders, including President Sheinbaum, criticized the governor's return as prioritizing personal ambition over party unity and state stability. Germany records over 14,000 heat-related deaths: Germany registered around 14,000 heat-related deaths this summer amid a series of heatwaves, official data showed, to AFP. Around 9,600 of those deaths took place in one week in late June when temperatures in Germany rose over 40 degrees Celsius (104 Fahrenheit), according to the Robert Koch Institute, which operates under the Federal Ministry of Health. DR Congo and M23 rebels agree on peace roadmap in Switzerland: Authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo said in a statement Saturday that the government and the Rwanda-backed M23 rebel group have established a roadmap for peace after five days of negotiations in Switzerland. Both sides committed to continuing talks and agreed to create a ceasefire monitoring mechanism, building on the 2025 U.S.-brokered peace framework. A monitoring team is scheduled for its first verification mission in South Kivu's Minembwe region. Despite the milestones, Drop Site correspondent , key disputes persist over detainee releases, political reforms, and sanctions on M23. Separately, DR Congo President Joseph Kabila is U.S. sanctions imposed over allegations that he supported the Rwanda-backed M23 rebellion. Kabila filed suit in federal court in Washington, D.C., seeking to overturn Treasury Department sanctions imposed April 30. He was sentenced to death in absentia by a Congolese military court in 2025 over ties to M23. Video shows hundreds held captive after mass abduction from Nigerian mosque: An armed group released a video what residents said were roughly 600 women, children, and elderly people abducted from a village in north-central Nigeria's Niger State over the weekend. Unidentified gunmen attacked worshippers during Friday prayers and simultaneously raided several surrounding communities, witnesses said, carrying the captives into a forest. No group has yet claimed responsibility for the attack though ransom kidnappings by criminal groups and extremists is common in the region and the fate of the abductees is presently unknown. | | ---|---|--- 🛒 for your Drop News/Not Bombs Hoodie 💬 our Whatsapp Broadcast Channel for the latest reporting, podcasts, and breaking news, delivered directly ⚠️ You can go to your to unsubscribe from the Drop Site Daily newsletter--while still getting the rest of our reporting Become a Drop Site News Paid Subscriber Drop Site News is reader-supported. name: Jasmine Clark
subject: Congress could use a Mad Scientist 😠🧑‍🔬
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jasmine Clark for Georgia Jasmine Clark for Georgia
body:
| | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137824876/642086686/-12840034?refcode=260824-MS-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NjYwMSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZTFmMDgzMi1kOTlmLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=bMTSyn4RubhUssXjCP9n5vUnUIm12AxXwA8xXGAy1Zg=)
---
| | | The night before Election Day in 2016, I was a pretty normal person. I was a mom, a professor, and a science nerd with a Ph.D. in microbiology. Then Donald Trump got elected, and I woke up a mad scientist. Before that, I spent my days in the lab. I studied bacteria, viruses, outbreaks, vaccines, and the things most people never see until they are suddenly making someone sick.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137824877/642086687/-12840034?refcode=260824-MS-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NjYwMSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZTFmMDgzMi1kOTlmLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=bMTSyn4RubhUssXjCP9n5vUnUIm12AxXwA8xXGAy1Zg=)
---
**And honestly? I loved it. ** I had no plans to run for office. I was happy doing research and teaching my students. But after Trump got elected, I saw the people in power not just ignoring science; they were mocking it. I realized I could either keep yelling at the TV or do something about it. **So I ran for the Georgia State Legislature to bring a scientist’s voice to the halls of the State Capitol.**
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137824878/642086688/-12840034?refcode=260824-MS-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NjYwMSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZTFmMDgzMi1kOTlmLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=bMTSyn4RubhUssXjCP9n5vUnUIm12AxXwA8xXGAy1Zg=)
---
Now it’s 2026, and somehow things have gotten crazier. **Trump and RFK Jr. are leading a full-scale assault on science** , vaccines, public health, and the experts who keep our families safe. **_That is why I am taking this fight to Congress._**
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137824879/642086689/-12840034?refcode=260824-MS-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NjYwMSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZTFmMDgzMi1kOTlmLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=bMTSyn4RubhUssXjCP9n5vUnUIm12AxXwA8xXGAy1Zg=)
---
Now it’s 2026, and somehow things have gotten crazier. **Trump and RFK Jr. are leading a full-scale assault on science** , vaccines, public health, and the experts who keep our families safe. **_That is why I am taking this fight to Congress._**
---
Because when Washington is overrun by conspiracy theories, junk science, and politicians who think public health is a punchline, we need someone at the table who actually understands the stakes. **We need a scientist.** **And yes, dare I say it: we need a mad scientist who is mad enough to do something about it. **
---

Then Donald Trump got elected, and I woke up a mad scientist. Before that, I spent my days in the lab. I studied bacteria, viruses, outbreaks, vaccines, and the things most people never see until they are suddenly making someone sick. = And honestly? I loved it. I had no plans to run for office. I was happy doing research and teaching my students. But after Trump got elected, I saw the people in power not just ignoring science; they were mocking it. I realized I could either keep yelling at the TV or do something about it. So I ran for the Georgia State Legislature to bring a scientist’s voice to the halls of the State Capitol. = Now it’s 2026, and somehow things have gotten crazier. Trump and RFK Jr. are leading a full-scale assault on science , vaccines, public health, and the experts who keep our families safe. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

#### _**[Powerful people are counting on us to forget. Endless Urgency exists to make sure we don't. We're building independent media that keeps the receipts, tells the truth, and refuses to move on just because the news cycle does. This work stays free for everyone because paid subscribers choose to sustain it. * * *
Folks,
There's a massive exodus of staff at every level of this administration. According to Politico this weekend, they're leaving because they know their best days are behind them. They know the midterms are going to be a bloodbath for Republicans. They know that once Democrats take the House -- and hopefully the Senate -- the investigations start in earnest. And they know the last two years of a Donald Trump who's further out of touch with reality and less popular by the minute is going to be a brutal place to work.
It would be easy for me to spike the football here. I feel it in my bones. I've been right a lot more than I've been wrong about how this second term was going to go.
But there's something more important than "I told you so," and it's a message I need every Republican in Washington -- and every staffer sprinting for the exits -- to hear clearly:
**Accountability is still coming for you.**
These people worked hand in hand with Donald Trump and his billionaire buddies to wreck the global economy, make your life worse, launch an illegal war, and steal billions of dollars from the American people. And now they think they can walk out the door, grab a corporate job, go back to running campaigns, and nothing will ever happen to them.
Screw that.
From Donald Trump and his family on down to people you've never heard of, this administration is full of people who broke and manipulated the law for their own personal and financial gain. The reckoning has to come. And Democrats need to understand that accountability isn't a distraction from winning the next two elections -- it's how you win them. It's how you set this country back on a path toward a government that works for us instead of a handful of corrupt billionaires and corporate lobbyists.
Which brings me to the other big story of the weekend: **Minority Leader Jeffries took a meeting with Jared Kushner.**
A lot of people are furious he took the meeting at all. I'm not one of them. I've always believed you meet with anybody. If Donald Trump called me tomorrow and said, "Mike, come to the White House," I'd be on the next flight to DC -- and I'd give him the same piece of my mind you'd get from me over a beer at the bar about the jackass in the Oval Office.
So my question isn't _why_ Hakeem took the meeting. My question is _what was discussed in it._ Because meeting with these people is one thing. Helping them escape accountability is something else entirely.
If there was any conversation -- any deal, any wink, any handshake -- about softening the accountability that's coming for Jared Kushner, for the crimes I believe he's committed and the money I believe he and his father-in-law and their family have stolen from the American people, that's a problem. If a deal was made to shield anyone inside the Trump crime family, I want to know about it, and we need to have that conversation out loud.
I have no reason to believe Hakeem would or did that. I'm just giving you my perspective -- and making clear what the standard has to be.
* * *
#### **[They're betting that eventually we'll stop paying attention. That's exactly why independent media like Endless Urgency matters. We can't hold powerful people accountable if we let them rewrite what happened the second the cameras move on. If you want to help us keep watching, keep documenting, and keep telling the truth long after everyone else has moved on, like, comment, share, and consider becoming a paid subscriber today. Just $8/month makes a huge difference:](https://substack.com/redirect/68d8ac63-4859-4b91-be37-1bc5f2c0fe8c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

* * *
Every single person in Washington needs to understand: the level of criminality and blatant corruption we are living through right now is unprecedented in modern American history. This is the kind of stuff that would make past corrupt administrations blush. Richard Nixon could not fathom it. The Grant or Harding administrations could not fathom it.
And it doesn't go away just because they leave office. It doesn't disappear because the news cycle moves on. I don't care how many pardons they hand out. I don't care where they hide the money. We should cast the widest possible net and claw back as much of our money and our democracy as humanly possible.
Kushner is the face of so much of this -- especially the manipulation of America's foreign policy apparatus for his own financial gain. The guy is literally building, alongside his wife, a new Epstein island, which has kicked off a massive international crisis. And they don't want to talk about it.
I'm tying these two stories together because we are through the looking glass. Trump's administration has already failed. All the bravado about the "golden age," all the confident talk from Republicans about the midterms -- it's play-acting. They have to get to the finish line too. And now the people around Trump are starting to think about what happens when this is over.
I've worked plenty of elections where I knew my candidate was going to lose, and I'm very good at coping when I need to. That's what Republicans are doing right now. It's cope.
And these rats fleeing the ship are doing it in the desperate hope that if they leave now, they'll be forgotten. That time will do them the favor of making everyone forget what they did and who they chose to serve when they had power.
But we will remember you. We will remember your character. We will remember the lies you told. We will remember what you did to weaken this nation abroad, to wreck the economy, to hurt working people who were already struggling, and to steal from people like you and me.
I told you the other day about my TV hit with Tricia McLaughlin, the former spokesperson for Trump's Department of Homeland Security. I remembered the lies she told, and when I called her out on them, she was flabbergasted. Because these people are used to this being pro wrestling. A daytime soap opera. You can say anything, do anything, hurt anyone -- and then everyone moves on to the next episode. They're counting on our attention spans being shorter than our memories.
We can't move on. If we don't remember, all of these people go quietly into the night for a little while, and then they come roaring back the next time there's a Republican administration -- to steal more money, hurt more people, break more laws, shatter more norms.
If we go back to sleep, it'll be no different than the Wall Street financial crisis. No different than the January 6th insurrectionists. No different than every other time we let people who committed heinous crimes walk right back into polite society like nothing happened.
Not this time. They're counting on us forgetting. Don't give them that. Eyes on the ball folks.
With urgency,
--Mike

Fellow Conservative,

This is not a warning anymore. It's already happening.

New York City has a socialist mayor.

| | Friend,
Our investigation into Dr. Fauci's government-issued phone is only just beginning, and I wanted you to hear the details directly from me.
My subcommittee, working alongside Senator Rand Paul's committee, has obtained a copy of Fauci's government iPhone from HHS. Here's what we've found so far:
✅ **More than 34,000 text messages**
✅ **522 voicemails**
✅ **Records spanning from 2014 to just days before Fauci left the NIH**
✅ **_And only 3 saved contacts, with nearly every other message tied only to a raw phone number, not a name_**
That last detail matters.
_When almost none of your correspondents are saved as actual contacts, despite tens of thousands of messages, it raises a simple question: was that an accident, or by design?_

This corrupt administration has said they’ve been investigating me for almost a year now. But there’s one small problem: **_They have absolutely nothing to investigate._**
But that doesn’t appease Trump’s MAGA fanatics, who were promised that I would be found guilty of crimes and deported out of the country.

He talked about fixing the economy. Now the cost of living crisis is worse than ever before.

subject: How much power do you have at work?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Claire Valdez for Congress](https://irrem7hbb
body:
Your boss gets a say. You deserve one too.
| | | | | [](https://irrem7hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001DnE0LY0oG8PcTZi86zul5Q1F9bhS79KiguGJEziykFl4f1zzUSdLYWpgZ8x-_oeRX1OFm5fRbb9_mKJlHcc0L77iMq44oOoml2AnRR6NwatnKFW_wBDa7aStfU1vFPpnQkVXG09wtkZcos4bDSovXcjuBGirkZSI4wH5xYymciOVwvEAn7bJdyc7hvzfVp8R-82e7rR9meF_oNQlkvLo7WJGiH1-xSgKfDiTW96gBTsFVAAieTQIOA==&c=VtPKzsIBJPy6HNSKn09uqGkinXcNEZDulreZjr-8AdKOaRK482zvtg==&ch=BfWcz041RO5OlbAcZp8YYTvowOeLgVVLWFbJxbDkPpyfzIez3NJtTg==)
---
| Almost everyone has a job, but almost no one has a union.
That's millions of people spending most of our waking lives in places where somebody else decides our pay, our schedule, and if we can speak up without risking everything.
I know how powerless that feels. I worked those bad jobs, spending years thinking the most I could hope for was making it to my next paycheck.
Then I joined my union, and for the first time in my working life, I didn't feel alone. My coworkers and I could sit across from our boss as equals and demand more.
That experience changed my entire life, and now I'm fighting to make sure every worker knows that kind of power.
[As I prepare to take this fight to Congress, I want to hear about your working life, what you wish you could change, and what would help you feel more powerful on the job. Will you take a few minutes to complete my Labor Survey?](https://irrem7hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001DnE0LY0oG8PcTZi86zul5Q1F9bhS79KiguGJEziykFl4f1zzUSdLYWpgZ8x-_oeRt05ED8Rf_PyiLoCz7zbUQWD0niBJLWZymRyzGUD-bOQ6Wfd8ZAc1mEi7feGayRRAYMqpMn-5KwxVAhqFnU4-xlJmvQjXTzvkGi_COuhBBYxA3S9R4FPw2RHxplWq8Qf73Q_io9xzuXuPGswMor5rfA83XOrjQpl1WtqNPAXyd5cuyCcmfbNjcnKCO0Sbo0Nm&c=VtPKzsIBJPy6HNSKn09uqGkinXcNEZDulreZjr-8AdKOaRK482zvtg==&ch=BfWcz041RO5OlbAcZp8YYTvowOeLgVVLWFbJxbDkPpyfzIez3NJtTg==)
---
| | [TAKE THE LABOR SURVEY](https://irrem7hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001DnE0LY0oG8PcTZi86zul5Q1F9bhS79KiguGJEziykFl4f1zzUSdLYWpgZ8x-_oeRt05ED8Rf_PyiLoCz7zbUQWD0niBJLWZymRyzGUD-bOQ6Wfd8ZAc1mEi7feGayRRAYMqpMn-5KwxVAhqFnU4-xlJmvQjXTzvkGi_COuhBBYxA3S9R4FPw2Z_656nppnb_AIbp1QZ-FvA=&c=VtPKzsIBJPy6HNSKn09uqGkinXcNEZDulreZjr-8AdKOaRK482zvtg==&ch=BfWcz041RO5OlbAcZp8YYTvowOeLgVVLWFbJxbDkPpyfzIez3NJtTg==)

| We spend too much of our lives working to accept poverty wages, unpredictable schedules, unsafe conditions, or a boss who treats us like we are disposable.
Workers deserve good pay, strong benefits and dignity on the job. And we really deserve a say over the conditions of our own lives.
Solidarity forever, Claire

I’m running for Congress to deliver new leadership for MN-08, and I need you with me. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will process immediately: = = = = = | | I’ve met thousands of voters across all 31,000 square miles of MN-08 over the course of this campaign so far, and I plan to meet many more over the next few months. We live in a truly remarkable district full of beautiful scenery and strong, resilient people. But our northern and central Minnesota communities are facing serious challenges that cannot go unaddressed: Many folks have to drive hours, even down to the Cities, for routine medical or dental care. Our local economy has stagnated, with countless young workers asking “what comes next?” Our famous lakes and wilderness areas are under threat from the most radically pro-polluter administration in our nation’s history. clean_body: | Friend, I’ve got to be honest: this is one of the toughest times of the year for a grassroots campaign like ours. People are soaking up the last few rays of summer sunshine, school is just around the corner, and families are spending extra quality time with each other before things get busy. I’m all in favor of it – but that also means that campaign donations tend to slow down. This is what we call the summer slump – the dreaded time where donations take a dip, and grassroots campaigns like ours begin to really feel the pinch. It happens every cycle – but this time is a bit different. With MI-08 being named “Seat 218” – the seat that could decide who controls Congress, every moment matters. Not an exaggeration! We simply can’t afford to slow down – not when National Republicans have already committed to spending over $2.5 million. And that’s only the beginning, friend. With President Trump ready to spend big and Elon Musk’s America PAC (yes, the same one that spent $1 million against me last cycle!) gearing up for a comeback – we must be prepared to fight back. = | | | = | = | | = | = | | = | = Thank you, Kristen | We'd hate to see you go, but you can click here if you'd like to . Thank you for supporting Kristen McDonald Rivet for Congress! Kristen for Michigan P.O. Box 854 Bay City, MI 48707 United States

* **Public opposition noted:** A May Gallup poll showed most Americans oppose data centers in their communities over environmental impact and large electricity and water needs.

# [Citi sees Nvidia soaring after blowout revenue outlook](https://substack.com/redirect/19078267-651a-4f84-992c-2d2b38b2aef1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Citi **[expects Nvidia to report July-quarter revenue of about $93 billion,](https://substack.com/redirect/33a678a9-1f63-41a4-af3b-9c4257574527?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** roughly $1 billion above estimates, driven by stronger B300 shipments and AI networking, while maintaining a Buy rating and $300 price target.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19078267-651a-4f84-992c-2d2b38b2aef1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Strong sequential growth:** Data-center revenue is forecast to rise 15% in the July quarter and 14% in October, exceeding Street expectations of 13% growth in both periods.
* **October outlook raised:** Citi projects October-quarter revenue of $105 billion, about $1.5 billion above consensus and representing a 13% sequential increase.
* **Blackwell shipment ramp:** Fiscal 2027 Blackwell GPU shipments are seen reaching 7.7 million units, while the Rubin estimate was lowered to 2 million units from 2.2 million.
* **Memory supply secured:** The firm believes Nvidia has secured sufficient high-bandwidth memory for 2026 and 2027, potentially allowing estimates to move higher.

# [Alibaba eyes $10.2 billion share sale to supercharge AI](https://substack.com/redirect/19078267-651a-4f84-992c-2d2b38b2aef1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Alibaba Group is **[seeking to raise about HK$80 billion or $10.2 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/bfe3682d-fd89-479d-aa58-19ca8572ab1b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** by offering 710 million shares at HK$112.7 each, a 3.6% discount, to fund full-stack AI capabilities and infrastructure expansion.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19078267-651a-4f84-992c-2d2b38b2aef1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Record Hong Kong deal:** The placement would be Hong Kong's biggest follow-on offering by a company on record and the city's biggest share sale since 2021.
* **Heavy AI spending:** Alibaba has ratcheted up quarterly capital spending to almost $10 billion amid competition for global AI leadership, with Qwen as the world's most popular model family.
* **Profit pressure shown:** June-quarter profit plunged more than 75% to 10.5 billion yuan or $1.6 billion, with a free-cash outflow of $6.6 billion from rising AI costs.
* **Lockup and arrangers:** The company faces a 90-day lockup, with arrangers including China International Capital, HSBC, Morgan Stanley and UBS.

# Treasury may unleash $1 trillion cash for massive bond buybacks
The U.S. Treasury is **[weighing use of its nearly $1 trillion General Account to fund expanded long-term bond buybacks,](https://substack.com/redirect/c5bc11a8-c459-4094-8034-9ed09f7dcea1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after doubling the maximum purchase size to at least $4 billion per operation.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ff5222b7-a169-4acf-a7f1-17619bc8937f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Account balance high:** The General Account stood near $950 billion, built by Secretary Scott Bessent using tax collections, well above the prior $550-600 billion target.
* **Buyback window set:** Larger operations for 10-to-30-year securities run from September 9 through November 4 after the August 19 announcement.
* **Funding via borrowing:** Purchases are funded through the Treasury General Account by taxes or new borrowing, treated as swapping one liability for another.
* **Debt load elevated:** The federal debt load sits at $40 trillion as the buyback program expands.

# [New Fed Chair Warsh's first Jackson Hole speech could rock markets](https://substack.com/redirect/19078267-651a-4f84-992c-2d2b38b2aef1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh **[will deliver his first speech at the Jackson Hole symposium](https://substack.com/redirect/30742357-6956-48c4-beb9-a57c39896559?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on Friday, with investors seeking clearer signals on inflation after long-term yields climbed to a two-decade high.

* **Rocky communications start:** Warsh has offered limited insight and avoided forward guidance since taking the role, drawing scrutiny after the July policy meeting.
* **Yields at highs:** Long-term bond yields reached a two-decade high after July comments, remaining elevated by sticky inflation and fiscal deficit concerns.
* **Inflation data focus:** Economists estimate the PCE price index rose 3.6% annually in July, the smallest increase in four months, as oil prices rise.
* **Reform task forces:** Five task forces are reviewing Fed operations including communications as Warsh faces pressure to clarify the reaction to inflation.

# [Walmart e-commerce explodes 23% as company raises outlook](https://substack.com/redirect/19078267-651a-4f84-992c-2d2b38b2aef1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Walmart reported **[global e-commerce sales rose 23% in the second quarter](https://substack.com/redirect/75ad0946-0a75-424b-b3e6-622c81ccff04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/75ad0946-0a75-424b-b3e6-622c81ccff04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)while U.S. e-commerce climbed 24%, driving revenue to $187.9 billion and prompting a raised full-year outlook.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19078267-651a-4f84-992c-2d2b38b2aef1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Revenue growth solid:** Second-quarter revenue reached $187.9 billion, up 5.9% from a year earlier, with strength in store-fulfilled delivery and marketplace.
**Sam 's Club boost:** Sam's Club U.S. e-commerce sales jumped 26% in the quarter, driven by club-fulfilled pickup and delivery options.
**CEO price pitch:** CEO John Furner said customers choose Walmart for price, speed and convenience across a broad assortment.
**Guidance raised:** The company raised its full-year outlook after the multi-year e-commerce growth showed a stronger and more durable business model.

# [Equal-weight S&P 500 ETF smashes $100 billion asset milestone](https://substack.com/redirect/19078267-651a-4f84-992c-2d2b38b2aef1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF **[surpassed $100 billion in assets under management for the first time](https://substack.com/redirect/f93ddc2b-c732-4ebb-bcc7-47784069f878?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** this month after attracting more than $12 billion in 2026.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19078267-651a-4f84-992c-2d2b38b2aef1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Outperformance clear:** The equal-weight approach outperformed the market-weight S&P 500 by roughly 3% year-to-date through August 21 amid broader market participation.
**Mag 7 concentration:** The Magnificent 7 make up roughly one-third of the S&P 500 and posted flat performance in the first half while the index gained 9.3%.
**Top 10 weight:** The top 10 names account for nearly 40% of the S&P 500, raising concentration risk concerns especially in AI themes.
**Diversification appeal:** Analysts note equal weighting solves concentration risk and lets investors participate if market leadership continues to broaden beyond mega-caps.

# [TikTok settles COPPA case with massive $400 million payout](https://substack.com/redirect/19078267-651a-4f84-992c-2d2b38b2aef1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
TikTok and ByteDance **[will pay $400 million to settle a Justice Department case](https://substack.com/redirect/1644ec76-be81-42de-9f5a-ef0db893c4d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** over Children's Online Privacy Protection Act violations, with $300 million due immediately.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19078267-651a-4f84-992c-2d2b38b2aef1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Payment structure set:** Of the $400 million total, $300 million is due immediately and $100 million upon vacating a prior Musical.ly consent decree.
* **Largest privacy cases:** The settlement ranks as one of the largest ever reached in a case involving the children's privacy act.
* **DOJ officials praise:** Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward called it a major victory for American children and parents.
* **Company changes noted:** Since the 2024 lawsuit, TikTok has altered ownership, management, compliance functions and privacy practices for younger users.

# Amazon's "toaster" robotaxis just started charging real fares
Amazon's Zoox **[toaster-shaped autonomous vehicles without steering wheels,](https://substack.com/redirect/22d98b9d-d1f1-4439-9fd5-b9ab2b63f0db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/22d98b9d-d1f1-4439-9fd5-b9ab2b63f0db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)dashboards or pedals have started charging for rides in Las Vegas while also operating across San Francisco as the first of their kind.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19078267-651a-4f84-992c-2d2b38b2aef1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **First Driverless Service:** The all-electric cars can drive in either direction and hold up to four passengers who sit facing each other, with windows stretching across much of the vehicle sides.
* **Robotaxi Market Outlook:** Goldman Sachs expects the growing robotaxi market to reach nearly $19 billion in sales by 2030 from $376 million last year as Amazon seeks major player status.
* **Regulatory Approval Limits:** The National Highway Transportation Safety Administration allowed Zoox to charge for rides in up to 5,000 vehicles over two years but restricted operations in heavy rain, snow or over 45 mph.
* **Fleet Size And Plans:** Zoox's current fleet of about 100 vehicles is assembled at a Hayward, California plant with capacity for 10,000 a year, with testing underway in Austin and Miami for soon service.

The Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF this month after attracting more than $12 billion in 2026. | | ---|---|--- Outperformance clear: The equal-weight approach outperformed the market-weight S&P 500 by roughly 3% year-to-date through August 21 amid broader market participation. Mag 7 concentration: The Magnificent 7 make up roughly one-third of the S&P 500 and posted flat performance in the first half while the index gained 9.3%. Top 10 weight: The top 10 names account for nearly 40% of the S&P 500, raising concentration risk concerns especially in AI themes. Diversification appeal: Analysts note equal weighting solves concentration risk and lets investors participate if market leadership continues to broaden beyond mega-caps. TikTok and ByteDance over Children's Online Privacy Protection Act violations, with $300 million due immediately. | | ---|---|--- Payment structure set: Of the $400 million total, $300 million is due immediately and $100 million upon vacating a prior Musical.ly consent decree. Largest privacy cases: The settlement ranks as one of the largest ever reached in a case involving the children's privacy act. DOJ officials praise: Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward called it a major victory for American children and parents. Company changes noted: Since the 2024 lawsuit, TikTok has altered ownership, management, compliance functions and privacy practices for younger users. Amazon's "toaster" robotaxis just started charging real fares Amazon's Zoox or pedals have started charging for rides in Las Vegas while also operating across San Francisco as the first of their kind. | | ---|---|--- First Driverless Service: The all-electric cars can drive in either direction and hold up to four passengers who sit facing each other, with windows stretching across much of the vehicle sides. Robotaxi Market Outlook: Goldman Sachs expects the growing robotaxi market to reach nearly $19 billion in sales by 2030 from $376 million last year as Amazon seeks major player status. Regulatory Approval Limits: The National Highway Transportation Safety Administration allowed Zoox to charge for rides in up to 5,000 vehicles over two years but restricted operations in heavy rain, snow or over 45 mph. Fleet Size And Plans: Zoox's current fleet of about 100 vehicles is assembled at a Hayward, California plant with capacity for 10,000 a year, with testing underway in Austin and Miami for soon service. We're behind where we should be, even though we've accomplished so much in just over 30 days. Just over four weeks ago, I officially got into this race. I am not a politician - and I think that's a good thing. My opponent has had 20 years to build up his campaign war chest. I have not. name: Michael Baumgartner
subject: Fresh from the Trail: This week's campaign update!

body:
Paint it Red, Riding the Red Wave through Lincoln and Pend Oreille County Fairs and the Pullman Lentil Festival!

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/NmHzWeloh_x?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
|
---
| |
# The Red Wave Starts NOW!
# Join us for “Paint it Red” Breakfast
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/dpgkrSEAMiU?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
| |
The primary is behind us and the red wave is just getting started. Join me for a high-energy **“Paint it Red”** breakfast on Thursday, August 27th, as we celebrate the win and lock in the momentum for November. We’re thrilled to welcome special guests Congressmen Randy Fine and Abe Hamadeh for an exclusive morning of breakfast, photos, and powerful conversation!
Whether you grab a VIP photo-line ticket or join us for the regular breakfast program, this is your chance to be part of the room that’s painting Eastern Washington Red! Spots are limited, so RSVP today and help us keep the wave rolling! To RSVP, call or text Anitra at 253-241-2420.
---
|
---
| |
# The Red Wave Doesn’t Take the Day Off
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/yt9IPidKFjS?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
| |

The primary win was just the starting gun, and Team Baumgartner is already hitting the ground running for the general election. We’re organizing our door-knocking efforts across Eastern Washington, planning sign-waving at busy intersections, ramping up phone calls, and getting ready to connect face-to-face with voters every single day.
The energy is real, the momentum is building, and the red wave is growing stronger by the day. The campaign is in full swing, and every conversation, every yard sign, and every door we knock is pushing us closer to victory in November. Now is the time to jump in and be part of it!! Sign up to volunteer [**here.**](https://us.list-manage.com/cn0yJrjgp7G?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
---
|
---
| |
# The Red Wave Rolled Through Pullman
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/QD7ha_4UTVm?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
| | I was proud to have our team represent the campaign at the Lentil Festival Parade in Pullman. Our volunteers and supporters walked the route with Baumgartner signs, waving to families, and connecting with folks from across Whitman County.
These community events matter and they’re where we meet voters face-to-face, listen to their concerns, and show that we’re all in for the general election in November. The energy in Pullman was strong, and it’s exactly the kind of grassroots momentum we need as we keep pushing forward!
---
|
---
| |
# Making Waves at the County Fairs:
# Lincoln and Pend Oreille
---
|
---
| | My team had a great time at both the Lincoln and Pend Oreille County Fairs and Rodeos. We connected with neighbors from across the county. From chatting with families near the livestock barns to visiting with folks at the Republican booth, it was a wonderful reminder of the strong, hardworking communities that make Eastern Washington special.
We appreciated the warm welcomes, the conversations about the issues that matter most to Lincoln County, and the chance to celebrate local agriculture, 4-H and FFA youth, and the classic fair spirit. Thank you to everyone who stopped by. It was a pleasure to be there with you!
---
|
---
|
---
| |
# Volunteer Spotlight: Randy
---
|
---
| |

This week we’re proud to spotlight Randy, a dedicated volunteer who faithfully makes calls for the campaign. Week after week, Randy reaches out to promote upcoming events and encourages people to get involved where they can. His steady commitment and positive attitude make a real difference in keeping our grassroots efforts strong. Thank you Randy, we’re grateful for everything you do!
---
|
---
| | More campaign signs will be going up over these next few weeks. _**Will you host a yard sign? **_Click [**here**](https://us.list-manage.com/19LNZoB9MhG?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238) to sign up now, or just send an email reply!We need volunteers! If you have a couple of hours to spare, please reach out to us! Visit our [**website**](https://us.list-manage.com/dSqGyhYSygU?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)**** to sign up now for opportunities, from attending parades or knocking on doors, to making phone calls or writing letters.**Upcoming Events** Team Baumgartner is on the move across Eastern Washington, connecting with neighbors and celebrating traditions that make our communities strong. Here is where you can find us next:
**Saturday August 29:** Northeast Washington Fair and Parade, Colville 10 am: Flags up, high-fives ready, and smiles on full blast as we parade through Colville. Come join us!
**Saturday September 5: **Walla Walla Fair and Frontier Days Parade, 10 am: Come join us and help mark the 160th anniversary of this great community celebration!
[T](https://us.list-manage.com/tMANo76Pbie?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)hank you for all your encouragement and support! -Michael
---

Friend, Sometimes people ask me: **_"How is a grassroots campaign supposed to beat a multi-million-dollar corporate machine?"_** _**Simple:**__** Look at who’s in our corner...**_ _We came to this fight as underdogs,_ and now– _neighbor by neighbor, county by county_ , we’ve built a movement that is _growing stronger every day. _ We aren't taking a single dime of corporate PAC money. Instead, _we’ve spent our time building a powerhouse coalition_ of _**everyday people, labor champions, and public servants**_ who are _ready to take back Tennessee. _**And that movement just got a whole lot stronger.** **I am _deeply honored_ to share that we’ve earned major new endorsements from leaders who have spent decades fighting for Tennessee workers and students:**

Dear Patriot,
Stand at that table with me for a second. Anchorage, Alaska. Primary day. A New York Post investigation has uncovered disturbing allegations surrounding Baoli Zhang, a 69-year-old owner of adult day care facilities in Flushing, Queens, whose businesses have billed Medicaid at least $32 million since 2018 while appearing suspiciously vacant to investigators. The report, published August 12, 2026, raises serious questions about oversight of taxpayer-funded healthcare programs and the cozy relationship between Medicaid providers and political donations in New York State.
According to the investigation, Zhang personally donated $10,000 to Governor Kathy Hochul's campaign, with an additional $5,000 contribution funneled through his Bao Kang Adult Day Care business. This pattern is not isolated: records show Hochul received approximately $55,000 in total campaign contributions from social adult daycare centers (SADCs) operating in fraud-plagued Flushing, Queens.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/03116bf6-ed5b-49ff-9138-2efec9e4274a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The most damning revelation emerged when New York Post reporters visited Bao Kang Adult Day Care at 132-29 Blossom Avenue. Despite the facility having billed Medicaid a staggering $31.8 million for serving 43,900 unique patients over a six-year period, the center appeared empty during the visit. The disconnect between the facility's massive Medicaid claims and its apparent lack of actual patients has drawn comparisons to broader patterns of fraud in the area.

This case is emblematic of a wider crisis in New York's Medicaid system. Federal investigators, reportedly led by Dr. Mehmet Oz, have intensified scrutiny of the state's Medicaid expenditures, which ballooned to $4,492 per resident in 2025. Flushing has emerged as a particular hotspot, with numerous social adult daycare centers often found empty while collectively billing Medicaid an estimated $100 million annually.
The investigation also uncovered troubling connections between these daycare facilities and local pharmacies. Community members have noted that many newer pharmacies in the area offer "benefits" and have established relationships with daycare centers, suggesting an ecosystem of incentives that may improperly lure patients and inflate claims. At least 60 to 70 percent of newer pharmacies are estimated to have connections to daycare operations.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/df1a4dd6-3213-423a-a01a-2f44e10c9b2e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Critics argue the political donations create a conflict of interest that discourages rigorous oversight. Health policy experts, including those at the Empire Center, contend that Governor Hochul and other top state officials rely heavily on political support and campaign contributions from Medicaid-funded healthcare providers, creating perverse incentives to suppress investigations rather than root out fraud.
The timing is particularly notable. Federal raids and heightened scrutiny of Medicaid fraud have put Democratic officials on the defensive. Governor Hochul has publicly denounced federal probes as politically motivated, but the documented connections between her campaign coffers and accused fraudsters complicate that narrative.
For New York taxpayers, the cost is substantial. With Zhang's businesses alone claiming $32 million for tens of thousands of patients while facilities sit empty, the scale of potential waste and fraud demands urgent accountability. The case highlights how campaign finance loopholes and lax regulatory oversight can combine to undermine public healthcare programs, diverting resources from vulnerable populations who genuinely need services.
Moving forward, the investigation will likely intensify pressure on state regulators to conduct independent audits of social adult daycare centers and examine the influence of healthcare provider donations on Albany's willingness to police its own Medicaid programs.

subject: Goodbye
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1811%2E1086043%2EhNsJef)
This is a longer email about saying goodbye, Peter, but if you don’t have time to read through, I would deeply appreciate **[a contribution to power our campaign.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260824-1.zg-LTq&refcode=em-20260824-1&t=2&akid=1811%2E1086043%2EhNsJef)**
After nearly a century of operation, Valley Forge Military Academy — the place where I went to school and grew from an angry, complicated child to a confident young man — has closed.
When my mother first sent me to the Forge, she saw military school as a last resort in response to a seemingly endless chain of misbehavior, both at home and at school. At age 11, I’d already felt handcuffs on my wrists. **I was not on a path to success.**
There was no overnight miracle when I started school there, but slowly, things changed. I learned about honor, code, and service. I started to take an interest in campus life, academics, and leadership positions — and I rose up the ranks and became a first captain in command of around 800 cadets.
After graduation, I went on to study at Johns Hopkins and Oxford, deployed to Afghanistan with the 82nd Airborne Division, ran one of the largest poverty-fighting organizations in the country, and now, I serve as the 63rd governor of Maryland _and the first Black governor in the history of my state._
What saddens me most isn’t losing a place I once called home. My memories will forever live on with me.
**It saddens me that other young men like me will have one fewer avenue to challenge themselves and build their own pathway to success.**
Peter, at a time where our young men and boys are falling behind and feeling isolated, we have to offer more paths for connection and engagement.
I know Valley Forge Military Academy did that for me, and I’m determined to find ways to do that for young Marylanders today.
That includes the **Maryland Corps and Service Year Option** — the first statewide program in the country to give high school graduates a year of paid, full-time community service on the path to college or a career.
We have to help young Marylanders find the thing that guides them on a pathway to success and that inspires them to serve. **[If you support that mission, I would appreciate a donation to keep me in the fight as Maryland's governor today.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260824-1.zg-LTq&refcode=em-20260824-1&t=3&akid=1811%2E1086043%2EhNsJef)**
Elevate,
Wes

When my mother first sent me to the Forge, she saw military school as a last resort in response to a seemingly endless chain of misbehavior, both at home and at school. At age 11, I’d already felt handcuffs on my wrists. I was not on a path to success. There was no overnight miracle when I started school there, but slowly, things changed. I learned about honor, code, and service. I started to take an interest in campus life, academics, and leadership positions — and I rose up the ranks and became a first captain in command of around 800 cadets. After graduation, I went on to study at Johns Hopkins and Oxford, deployed to Afghanistan with the 82nd Airborne Division, ran one of the largest poverty-fighting organizations in the country, and now, I serve as the 63rd governor of Maryland and the first Black governor in the history of my state. What saddens me most isn’t losing a place I once called home. My memories will forever live on with me. It saddens me that other young men like me will have one fewer avenue to challenge themselves and build their own pathway to success. Peter, at a time where our young men and boys are falling behind and feeling isolated, we have to offer more paths for connection and engagement. I know Valley Forge Military Academy did that for me, and I’m determined to find ways to do that for young Marylanders today. That includes the Maryland Corps and Service Year Option — the first statewide program in the country to give high school graduates a year of paid, full-time community service on the path to college or a career. We have to help young Marylanders find the thing that guides them on a pathway to success and that inspires them to serve. Peter, Nebraska's 2nd Congressional District, home to Omaha, the state's largest city, is a "blue dot" in a red state. It is one of just eight districts nationwide that elected a Republican to Congress while also backing Kamala Harris for president.
The Republican incumbent is retiring, leaving an open congressional seat for the first time in a decade. Democratic candidate Denise Powell is running to flip it, facing off against Trump endorsed MAGA extremist and Omaha City Councilman Brinker Harding.
Flipping this seat will help get Democrats to the exact math needed to take back the House majority.
