The purpose behind all of it is simple. We want visitors, especially young people, to walk out believing they could be the next entrepreneur, not just admirers of those who came before them. That belief is the whole point.

Somewhere in America right now, a kid is tinkering with something in a garage the same way Franklin once did, wondering if they could really be an entrepreneur too.

**Hall of Giants is how we make sure that kid grows up believing the story includes people like them.**

Every dollar helps us tell these stories the way they deserve to be told, with the wonder, the craftsmanship, and the honesty they've earned, warts and all, because the failures are as much a part of an entrepreneur's story as the wins.

A country only keeps producing entrepreneurs if its people believe that path is still open to them, and right now, too many young people have quietly decided it isn't.

Hall of Giants is how we hand that belief back to them.

But an institution like this doesn't come together on excitement alone. It takes people willing to invest early in something they believe in, the same risk every entrepreneur in this story once took.

clean_body: Friend, Before Ben Franklin helped write the Declaration of Independence, before he represented a new nation in the courts of Europe, he was something simpler and, in some ways, more remarkable. He was an inventor. The lightning rod. The bifocal lens. A stove that heated homes more efficiently than anything before it. And many more everyday items! Franklin never patented a single one of these creations, because he believed the whole point of a good idea was to share it with the world. That single instinct, that a person with curiosity and grit could improve the lives of total strangers, made him the first American to become a celebrity for what he created rather than the title he held. Benjamin Franklin wasn 't a statesman who happened to invent things on the side. He was, at his core, an entrepreneur. Someone who saw a problem, risked his time and reputation on a solution, and put it into the world without waiting for permission. Since Franklin, our country has been carried forward by entrepreneurs who looked at a problem and decided they were the ones to solve it. Thomas Edison bet everything on an idea most people thought was impossible. Henry Ford risked his name on a vision for how ordinary families would live and move. A generation later, entrepreneurs launching rockets, writing software, and reimagining the car are chasing that same instinct, the belief that if you see the future clearly enough, you can go out and make it. This is the story Hall of Giants exists to tell, and it's a story we believe America has stopped telling well. Even worse, some exhibits, like the one currently at the Smithsonian, have leaned toward reducing entrepreneurs like Benjamin Franklin to a list of flaws. Hall of Giants was founded to give visitors something better, a real human being worth arguing about and worth admiring at the same time. Hall of Giants is a new cultural institution, closer to Disneyland than a traditional museum, dedicated entirely to the entrepreneur. Instead of static exhibits and placards, visitors step directly into the moments when someone decided to bet on themselves. They walk into the garage, where an idea first took shape. They stand on the factory floor where a risk finally paid off. They ride all the way to the bell at the Nasdaq, tracing the full arc of what it actually takes to go from an idea nobody believed in to a legacy that outlives its founder. Every exhibit is designed to be lived in and argued with, not just looked at. This summer, we've been watching that same curiosity show up in a way we didn't fully expect. Hall of Giants has been touring the country with a life-size hologram of Benjamin Franklin, and it has been captivating people everywhere it goes. Visitors don't just look at him. They talk to him. They ask him about his inventions, his role in the Founding, and the ideas that made him a household name in his own lifetime. But they don't stop there. They ask him about his views on slavery, on women's suffrage, on the political flashpoints of his era, and they listen closely to how he answers. What we've noticed is something we think says a lot about the country right now. The average American standing in front of that hologram doesn't fall into uncritical admiration, nor into knee-jerk vilification. They hold his whole life in their hands at once, the genius and the contradictions together, and they come away with a fuller, more honest picture of the man. That instinct, to look clearly at a real, complicated person and still find something worth celebrating, is exactly the instinct Hall of Giants wants to encourage. The purpose behind all of it is simple. We want visitors, especially young people, to walk out believing they could be the next entrepreneur, not just admirers of those who came before them. That belief is the whole point. Somewhere in America right now, a kid is tinkering with something in a garage the same way Franklin once did, wondering if they could really be an entrepreneur too. Hall of Giants is how we make sure that kid grows up believing the story includes people like them. Every dollar helps us tell these stories the way they deserve to be told, with the wonder, the craftsmanship, and the honesty they've earned, warts and all, because the failures are as much a part of an entrepreneur's story as the wins. A country only keeps producing entrepreneurs if its people believe that path is still open to them, and right now, too many young people have quietly decided it isn't. Hall of Giants is how we hand that belief back to them. But an institution like this doesn't come together on excitement alone. It takes people willing to invest early in something they believe in, the same risk every entrepreneur in this story once took. The Israeli Ministry of Defense and Israeli defense companies have directed millions in unreported funding to U.S. university research programs for weapons development, sponsoring research directly or serving as the pass-through entity for the funding, a Drop Site investigation has found.
A sample of state and university audits, foreign-funding disclosures, and other institutional records identified millions of dollars in financial ties over the last two decades between the Israeli Ministry of Defense (MOD), Israeli weapons manufacturers, and American universities, much of which does not appear consistently in national databases intended to track foreign funding into U.S. universities.
An analysis of audit records, building on findings compiled by the [Antiwar Initiative](https://substack.com/redirect/3f6cb69e-71d6-4757-b17a-968f03379c5a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), an academic research group that documents the connections between universities and the global arms industry, found more than $15 million of unreported or inconsistently reported entries for funding tied to the Israeli MOD or defense manufacturers.
The true scale of Israeli support is difficult to determine because entries for such funding were often not reported in public filings mandating disclosure of foreign gifts, but were discovered by manually cross-referencing public and internal databases, audit records, and acknowledgments in academic papers. Some projects listed in university materials as being sponsored by the Israeli MOD or defense companies also did not include the amounts of funding provided, or contained inconsistent or contradictory records in audit databases.
Drop Site reviewed and verified public records that showed research grants, tuition payments, and receipts of gifts totalling millions of dollars to dozens of colleges and universities around the country. The data shows examples of financial support and sponsorship for American researchers from the Israeli Ministry of Defense as well as Israeli weapons manufacturers like Elbit Systems.
Records dating from 2004 to 2025 point to a large number of schools that have had financial relationships with the Israeli MOD or Israeli weapons manufacturers, including Columbia, Cornell, Princeton, Harvard, Northwestern, Georgia Tech, Texas Tech, the University of Connecticut, the University of Tennessee, the University of Maryland, the University of Florida, the University of California at Berkeley, the University of Rhode Island, the University of New Mexico, the Washington University in St. Louis, and the State University of New York.
The recorded financial relationships include time-bound research contracts and do not indicate whether relationships with the MOD are still ongoing. Previous reporting has documented MOD funding of programs at MIT and student protests there over the relationship.
In addition to financial support from the MOD and Elbit, records also showed sponsorship of individual research projects related to military technologies by Israeli defense manufacturers Rafael and Israel Aerospace Industries.
Taken together, the records reveal an opaque defense-research pipeline spread across some of the country's most prominent universities.
In one example that illustrates the typical nature of these ties, an Israeli MOD-sponsored [project](https://substack.com/redirect/bcdacbe8-29bb-44d7-bc0b-3ee4a97c9ee9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at the University of Connecticut was listed in [public audit records](https://substack.com/redirect/1992fcb7-5447-4670-a6ec-29a788b9eed9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with the title, "Impact Point Prediction Research for Short & Medium Range Thrusting Projectiles."
Connecticut's annual federal-award schedules record $668,456 in funding under that title across nine fiscal years between 2013 and 2023 with the funder listed as Israel's Ministry of Defense. Another Israeli MOD-linked research project at the school titled, "High Sensitivity SQUIDs for Magnetic Field Detection," received $251,336 in funding across the same time period.
Federal law requires colleges and universities receiving federal assistance to disclose gifts and contracts totaling at least $250,000 in a calendar year from a foreign source, though transactions below that threshold may remain outside the public reporting system. But these multi-year contributions do not consistently appear in federal databases intended to help the public track foreign money flowing into American universities. The Education Department's latest[ public disclosure](https://substack.com/redirect/ade51106-f9d4-4873-9a64-e1d0b620c1f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of foreign gifts and funding contains no Israel-attributed entry for the University of Connecticut, even as entries for MOD funding show up in other databases and audit documentation.
The Israeli government and its allies in Congress are now seeking to transform relationships like these from a scattered research pipeline into formal American defense policy. The fiscal 2026 National Defense Authorization Act already[ directed the Pentagon](https://substack.com/redirect/fc169201-f301-49c4-bf82-c88b627ac23b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to establish a U.S.-Israel Defense Industrial Base Working Group to consider integrating Israel into what it calls "the American National Technology and Industrial Base."
A proposal advanced by the House Armed Services Committee for the fiscal 2027 NDAA would go further, creating a[ United States-Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Initiative](https://substack.com/redirect/f5af1c9d-2645-4c8c-9466-a95d4bf4c85d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) charged with expanding bilateral research, development, testing, weapons production, and industrial cooperation. If these measures become law, the scattered funding connections documented in American university audit trails and research papers would become part of the architecture of the American military-industrial base.
## **Gears of War**
Israeli forces have used drones, automated intelligence tools, persistent aerial surveillance, precision-guided projectiles, and large-scale data analysis throughout the genocide in the Gaza Strip, as well as wars in Lebanon, Iran, Syria, and Yemen.
Those operations draw upon the technologies originating in the same research fields that the Israeli government and weapons manufacturers have paid American academics to advance: video surveillance, human-activity recognition, autonomous flight, network analysis, target identification, magnetic sensing, and projectile impact modeling. At the University of Central Florida, researchers have received[ funding from Elbit Systems](https://substack.com/redirect/7ebb789f-79ef-45aa-b6bd-e3060f59458e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to develop algorithms to recognize human activity and detect objects in video.
Records from the University of Tennessee show that a U.S. subsidiary of Elbit also provided $514,500 in payments to the school between[ 2023](https://substack.com/redirect/c3015f8d-9974-4e7c-abf2-f380ceffecba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg),[ 2024](https://substack.com/redirect/c8907deb-f798-4573-8084-88cc1404937b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and[ 2025](https://substack.com/redirect/e9b6ac54-2baf-46a9-a68e-c89e0484faf6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The available public documentation does not identify what programs or researchers the contributions are intended to support, with the description listing the purpose of the funding as simply "tuition payments for various students."
"For relatively small sums--like the price of funding a single PhD--Israel has gained major new capabilities that have bolstered its capacity to commit genocide in Gaza, carry out a brutal occupation of Lebanon, and spark a war with Iran that has escalated to a region wide conflict," said William Hartung, a political scientist and expert on the U.S. arms industry and Pentagon budgetary practices.
Many awards from the Israeli MOD are classified as U.S. Department of Defense expenditures, with the Israeli ministry identified as the pass-through entity that administers the grants. MIT, for example, has[ stated](https://substack.com/redirect/94ae5bad-3074-4adc-a03c-9a4405990257?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the money for its projects funded by the Israeli ministry originated with the U.S. Department of Defense. The U.S. provides an estimated $3.8 billion in annual military aid to Israel on top of other forms of assistance.
Some audit records identify the Pentagon's Defense Security Cooperation Agency, which administers U.S. security assistance and weapons-transfer programs, as the primary agency providing the funding that was ultimately directed by the Israeli MOD. The public documents do not establish whether every dollar for particular research support at a school came from Israel's treasury, from U.S. military assistance placed under Israeli procurement authority, or from some combination of the two.
## **Audit Trail**
In the summer of 2025, MIT professor Markus Buehler withdrew from an Israeli Defense Ministry grant after a student-led campaign publicized the project. The decision followed more than a year of protests over MIT's defense relationships with Israel, which the university[ says amounted to $4 million](https://substack.com/redirect/94ae5bad-3074-4adc-a03c-9a4405990257?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for individual ministry-linked projects between fiscal 2015 and fiscal 2024, plus $290,000 in fiscal 2025.
A trail of open source records traces similar financial and research relationships between the Israeli defense establishment and schools in Connecticut, New York, Maryland, Florida, New Jersey, Texas, California, and Virginia.
At Columbia University, annual audits name two ministry-linked projects and record $799,190 in grants. One MOD-funded project for "Direct 3D Printing of Integrated Electro Mechanical Systems" accounted for $469,999 from 2016 through 2021, while another for "Optimizing Micro Resonators Based Sensor" accounted for another $329,191 from 2021 through 2024. Columbia's[ fiscal 2024 audit](https://substack.com/redirect/36de242c-d706-4b1f-88b1-c6af9694d578?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) lists the latter project under the U.S. Department of Defense, with the "Israeli Ministry of Defense" as the "pass-through name," and records $25,327 in funding.
The Research Foundation for the State University of New York shows audit entries for five Israeli MOD-linked projects[ totaling](https://substack.com/redirect/ca63194a-c33a-4577-811b-2b12457c8258?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) $949,915 from 2010 through 2021.
Florida's statewide audits record $1,195,795 in expenditures passed through the Ministry of Defense from 2012 through 2021, while not identifying the schools that received all of this funding.
Campus records connect at least some of the awards to the University of Central Florida and the University of Florida. One University of Florida engineering[ publication](https://substack.com/redirect/f8b3a4b3-2edb-4783-bf0e-5f58f49cb29b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) names an Israeli MOD-sponsored project, "Coupled Size and Rate Effects in Ultra-High-Performance Concrete," beginning in 2012. While listing the project under "Sponsored Research," the newsletter did not identify the amount the school received from the MOD for the study.
In response to a request for comment about another $150,000 contract beginning in March 2015 that named the Israeli Ministry of Defense at UC Berkeley, a spokesperson said that, "UC Berkeley complies with all of the statues and regulations that apply to contracts and gifts from foreign sources," noting that the school is only involved in fundamental research and adding that, "every government, every researcher, every person in the world is able to read the results of our research in freely available scientific publications."
UC Berkeley did not respond to additional questions about the purpose of the MOD funding. Other schools contacted by Drop Site did not respond to requests for comment or stated that they could not provide information about the cited funding.
In addition to records from audits, public information from individual researchers provides more hints of the scope of Israeli military's U.S. research funding.
In February,[ The Nation reported](https://substack.com/redirect/7ebb789f-79ef-45aa-b6bd-e3060f59458e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that computer-vision researchers Mubarak Shah and Abhijit Mahalanobis received a $200,000 Elbit Systems of America grant in 2020 to develop "human activity recognition" technology, while Mahalanobis received another $60,000 for algorithms involving object detection and human-activity recognition.
At the University of Maryland, aerospace engineering professor Inderjit Chopra's[ research page](https://substack.com/redirect/b03a3956-2829-4c0f-b87d-a49a2037a263?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) lists two Israeli ministry grants: $150,000 for "Autonomous Operation of Micro-Helicopters," from 2011 to 2012, and $300,000 for "Aeromechanics of Rotorcraft in High Speed Flight," from 2014 to 2016.
A curriculum vitae[ filed](https://substack.com/redirect/1874ae1c-efd0-4630-86df-64b245083d12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by another researcher in a separate U.S. Patent and Trademark Office proceeding lists Israeli MOD funding of $150,000 for "Functional Targeting of Terror Networks: A Big Data Approach," from February 2017 through December 2018, and $153,520 for "Fast Algorithms for Group Between-ness Centrality in Massive Social Networks."
Princeton University records identify physicist Michael Romalis on a $600,000 contract called "Pulsed Scalar Atomic Magnetometer." The university's fiscal 2018 sponsored-awards[ report](https://substack.com/redirect/395953a4-f5cd-4c01-a980-2251955fc33c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) names the Government of Israel's Ministry of Defense and the Defense Security Cooperation Agency as sponsors and gives a contract period from July 2015 through June 2019.
Texas Tech University's engineering newsletters list yet another award for $400,000 from the Israeli Defense Ministry to research a "Sealed Vircator HPM System," naming James Dickens, John Mankowski, and Andreas Neuber as researchers. The same amount and title appear in both the[ January 2014](https://substack.com/redirect/d36e2cca-d098-4286-90e0-6b3d400aaf7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and[ April 2015](https://substack.com/redirect/a86fbdaa-f680-45c9-810b-24335721e9a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) newsletters.
The vircator technology has a clear military application: Texas Tech's Center for Pulsed Power and Power Electronics[ describes](https://substack.com/redirect/403a3ec2-42b1-4c14-b49a-8b9db1ab234c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) vircators as compact, high-power microwave sources and says its work includes coordinating vehicle-mounted emitters with GPS timing to place a microwave "hot spot" at a desired location--an application potentially useful for combatting drone swarms.
The purpose of a separate Israeli Defense Ministry-linked funding stream at the University of Texas at Austin is less clear from the public records. UT Austin's fiscal 2013 financial report[ identifies](https://substack.com/redirect/b763b9ca-b211-470e-bc64-bcea4e03a478?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) $58,992 in expenditures under an Israeli Ministry of Defense purchase order. Statewide audit schedules record expenditures under the same purchase order reappearing in public audit records from 2010 through 2014, for a total of $299,952.
The audit archive contains still more Israeli military-named expenditures, including recorded contributions to[ Northwestern University](https://substack.com/redirect/93868169-bcd5-4896-acb5-b1ab2e0bdcaf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [Washington University in St. Louis](https://substack.com/redirect/c3947098-abcd-484c-8011-564aab927977?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and repeated entries for the MOD in [audits](https://substack.com/redirect/26b70a52-3b79-4c4b-8e1f-c17eecfd0996?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for the state of Virginia.
But the opaque nature of some support that turned up in public records means that financial and in-kind support to universities may not even be recorded in any audit trail at all.
At the University of Texas at Dallas, Haoran Wei and Nasser Kehtarnavaz produced a video-surveillance system in a study that the[ published](https://substack.com/redirect/9d033cf0-6386-42f7-9cfb-4bbdc1ad83fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) paper indicated was "funded by Elbit Systems of America through a contract with the University of Texas at Dallas" without mentioning the amount of financial support. The report also noted that the company had provided "far-field video clips" to help conduct their research on target recognition.
The researchers did not respond to requests for comment about the nature of their work and ties to Elbit.
## **Disclosure Gap**
Section 117 of the[ Higher Education Act](https://substack.com/redirect/d21e9ba6-c469-4cb2-9560-fd4e71f26f5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) generally requires a federally assisted university to report covered gifts and contracts from a foreign source when they meet or exceed $250,000, including multi-year contracts meeting that threshold over their duration. Under the Education Department's example, a five-year research contract worth $50,000 a year is reportable at signing because its lifetime value is $250,000.
The Education Department's inspector general[ warned](https://substack.com/redirect/6ae51747-850a-4ff6-8552-992c22d86f0e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in February 2025 that oversight of the system was weak with insufficient controls to ensure reporting requirements were being met. The current disclosure thresholds also make it easier for foreign countries to contribute amounts below that number to avoid triggering reporting requirements but can be significant for individual research projects.
That lack of oversight contributes to a situation in which millions of dollars from a foreign military under increasing scrutiny in the U.S. for human rights abuses and facing genocide charges from international courts has been able to spend millions of dollars funding military research at American universities.
These relationships are now coming under greater scrutiny at a time when public opinion on Israel has soured in the U.S. due to the genocide in Gaza and Israeli conduct in other regional conflicts.
"No self-respecting university should accept funding from Israel, given its destabilizing, destructive, and inhumane use of U.S. weapons," said Hartung.

The Israeli Ministry of Defense and Israeli defense companies have directed millions in unreported funding to U.S. university research programs for weapons development, sponsoring research directly or serving as the pass-through entity for the funding, a Drop Site investigation has found. A sample of state and university audits, foreign-funding disclosures, and other institutional records identified millions of dollars in financial ties over the last two decades between the Israeli Ministry of Defense (MOD), Israeli weapons manufacturers, and American universities, much of which does not appear consistently in national databases intended to track foreign funding into U.S. universities. An analysis of audit records, building on findings compiled by the , an academic research group that documents the connections between universities and the global arms industry, found more than $15 million of unreported or inconsistently reported entries for funding tied to the Israeli MOD or defense manufacturers. The true scale of Israeli support is difficult to determine because entries for such funding were often not reported in public filings mandating disclosure of foreign gifts, but were discovered by manually cross-referencing public and internal databases, audit records, and acknowledgments in academic papers. Some projects listed in university materials as being sponsored by the Israeli MOD or defense companies also did not include the amounts of funding provided, or contained inconsistent or contradictory records in audit databases. Drop Site reviewed and verified public records that showed research grants, tuition payments, and receipts of gifts totalling millions of dollars to dozens of colleges and universities around the country. The data shows examples of financial support and sponsorship for American researchers from the Israeli Ministry of Defense as well as Israeli weapons manufacturers like Elbit Systems. Records dating from 2004 to 2025 point to a large number of schools that have had financial relationships with the Israeli MOD or Israeli weapons manufacturers, including Columbia, Cornell, Princeton, Harvard, Northwestern, Georgia Tech, Texas Tech, the University of Connecticut, the University of Tennessee, the University of Maryland, the University of Florida, the University of California at Berkeley, the University of Rhode Island, the University of New Mexico, the Washington University in St. Louis, and the State University of New York. The recorded financial relationships include time-bound research contracts and do not indicate whether relationships with the MOD are still ongoing. Previous reporting has documented MOD funding of programs at MIT and student protests there over the relationship. In addition to financial support from the MOD and Elbit, records also showed sponsorship of individual research projects related to military technologies by Israeli defense manufacturers Rafael and Israel Aerospace Industries. Taken together, the records reveal an opaque defense-research pipeline spread across some of the country's most prominent universities. In one example that illustrates the typical nature of these ties, an Israeli MOD-sponsored at the University of Connecticut was listed in with the title, "Impact Point Prediction Research for Short & Medium Range Thrusting Projectiles." Connecticut's annual federal-award schedules record $668,456 in funding under that title across nine fiscal years between 2013 and 2023 with the funder listed as Israel's Ministry of Defense. Another Israeli MOD-linked research project at the school titled, "High Sensitivity SQUIDs for Magnetic Field Detection," received $251,336 in funding across the same time period. Federal law requires colleges and universities receiving federal assistance to disclose gifts and contracts totaling at least $250,000 in a calendar year from a foreign source, though transactions below that threshold may remain outside the public reporting system. But these multi-year contributions do not consistently appear in federal databases intended to help the public track foreign money flowing into American universities. The Education Department's latest of foreign gifts and funding contains no Israel-attributed entry for the University of Connecticut, even as entries for MOD funding show up in other databases and audit documentation. The Israeli government and its allies in Congress are now seeking to transform relationships like these from a scattered research pipeline into formal American defense policy. The fiscal 2026 National Defense Authorization Act already to establish a U.S.-Israel Defense Industrial Base Working Group to consider integrating Israel into what it calls "the American National Technology and Industrial Base." A proposal advanced by the House Armed Services Committee for the fiscal 2027 NDAA would go further, creating a charged with expanding bilateral research, development, testing, weapons production, and industrial cooperation. If these measures become law, the scattered funding connections documented in American university audit trails and research papers would become part of the architecture of the American military-industrial base. Gears of War Israeli forces have used drones, automated intelligence tools, persistent aerial surveillance, precision-guided projectiles, and large-scale data analysis throughout the genocide in the Gaza Strip, as well as wars in Lebanon, Iran, Syria, and Yemen. Those operations draw upon the technologies originating in the same research fields that the Israeli government and weapons manufacturers have paid American academics to advance: video surveillance, human-activity recognition, autonomous flight, network analysis, target identification, magnetic sensing, and projectile impact modeling. At the University of Central Florida, researchers have received to develop algorithms to recognize human activity and detect objects in video. Records from the University of Tennessee show that a U.S. subsidiary of Elbit also provided $514,500 in payments to the school between, and. The available public documentation does not identify what programs or researchers the contributions are intended to support, with the description listing the purpose of the funding as simply "tuition payments for various students." "For relatively small sums--like the price of funding a single PhD--Israel has gained major new capabilities that have bolstered its capacity to commit genocide in Gaza, carry out a brutal occupation of Lebanon, and spark a war with Iran that has escalated to a region wide conflict," said William Hartung, a political scientist and expert on the U.S. arms industry and Pentagon budgetary practices. Many awards from the Israeli MOD are classified as U.S. Department of Defense expenditures, with the Israeli ministry identified as the pass-through entity that administers the grants. MIT, for example, has that the money for its projects funded by the Israeli ministry originated with the U.S. Department of Defense. The U.S. provides an estimated $3.8 billion in annual military aid to Israel on top of other forms of assistance. Some audit records identify the Pentagon's Defense Security Cooperation Agency, which administers U.S. security assistance and weapons-transfer programs, as the primary agency providing the funding that was ultimately directed by the Israeli MOD. The public documents do not establish whether every dollar for particular research support at a school came from Israel's treasury, from U.S. military assistance placed under Israeli procurement authority, or from some combination of the two. Audit Trail In the summer of 2025, MIT professor Markus Buehler withdrew from an Israeli Defense Ministry grant after a student-led campaign publicized the project. The decision followed more than a year of protests over MIT's defense relationships with Israel, which the university for individual ministry-linked projects between fiscal 2015 and fiscal 2024, plus $290,000 in fiscal 2025. A trail of open source records traces similar financial and research relationships between the Israeli defense establishment and schools in Connecticut, New York, Maryland, Florida, New Jersey, Texas, California, and Virginia. At Columbia University, annual audits name two ministry-linked projects and record $799,190 in grants. One MOD-funded project for "Direct 3D Printing of Integrated Electro Mechanical Systems" accounted for $469,999 from 2016 through 2021, while another for "Optimizing Micro Resonators Based Sensor" accounted for another $329,191 from 2021 through 2024. Columbia's lists the latter project under the U.S. Department of Defense, with the "Israeli Ministry of Defense" as the "pass-through name," and records $25,327 in funding. The Research Foundation for the State University of New York shows audit entries for five Israeli MOD-linked projects $949,915 from 2010 through 2021. Florida's statewide audits record $1,195,795 in expenditures passed through the Ministry of Defense from 2012 through 2021, while not identifying the schools that received all of this funding. Campus records connect at least some of the awards to the University of Central Florida and the University of Florida. One University of Florida engineering names an Israeli MOD-sponsored project, "Coupled Size and Rate Effects in Ultra-High-Performance Concrete," beginning in 2012. While listing the project under "Sponsored Research," the newsletter did not identify the amount the school received from the MOD for the study. In response to a request for comment about another $150,000 contract beginning in March 2015 that named the Israeli Ministry of Defense at UC Berkeley, a spokesperson said that, "UC Berkeley complies with all of the statues and regulations that apply to contracts and gifts from foreign sources," noting that the school is only involved in fundamental research and adding that, "every government, every researcher, every person in the world is able to read the results of our research in freely available scientific publications." UC Berkeley did not respond to additional questions about the purpose of the MOD funding. Other schools contacted by Drop Site did not respond to requests for comment or stated that they could not provide information about the cited funding. In addition to records from audits, public information from individual researchers provides more hints of the scope of Israeli military's U.S. research funding. In February, that computer-vision researchers Mubarak Shah and Abhijit Mahalanobis received a $200,000 Elbit Systems of America grant in 2020 to develop "human activity recognition" technology, while Mahalanobis received another $60,000 for algorithms involving object detection and human-activity recognition. At the University of Maryland, aerospace engineering professor Inderjit Chopra's lists two Israeli ministry grants: $150,000 for "Autonomous Operation of Micro-Helicopters," from 2011 to 2012, and $300,000 for "Aeromechanics of Rotorcraft in High Speed Flight," from 2014 to 2016. A curriculum vitae by another researcher in a separate U.S. Patent and Trademark Office proceeding lists Israeli MOD funding of $150,000 for "Functional Targeting of Terror Networks: A Big Data Approach," from February 2017 through December 2018, and $153,520 for "Fast Algorithms for Group Between-ness Centrality in Massive Social Networks." Princeton University records identify physicist Michael Romalis on a $600,000 contract called "Pulsed Scalar Atomic Magnetometer." The university's fiscal 2018 sponsored-awards names the Government of Israel's Ministry of Defense and the Defense Security Cooperation Agency as sponsors and gives a contract period from July 2015 through June 2019. Texas Tech University's engineering newsletters list yet another award for $400,000 from the Israeli Defense Ministry to research a "Sealed Vircator HPM System," naming James Dickens, John Mankowski, and Andreas Neuber as researchers. The same amount and title appear in both the and newsletters. The vircator technology has a clear military application: Texas Tech's Center for Pulsed Power and Power Electronics vircators as compact, high-power microwave sources and says its work includes coordinating vehicle-mounted emitters with GPS timing to place a microwave "hot spot" at a desired location--an application potentially useful for combatting drone swarms. The purpose of a separate Israeli Defense Ministry-linked funding stream at the University of Texas at Austin is less clear from the public records. UT Austin's fiscal 2013 financial report $58,992 in expenditures under an Israeli Ministry of Defense purchase order. Statewide audit schedules record expenditures under the same purchase order reappearing in public audit records from 2010 through 2014, for a total of $299,952. The audit archive contains still more Israeli military-named expenditures, including recorded contributions to and , and repeated entries for the MOD in for the state of Virginia. But the opaque nature of some support that turned up in public records means that financial and in-kind support to universities may not even be recorded in any audit trail at all. At the University of Texas at Dallas, Haoran Wei and Nasser Kehtarnavaz produced a video-surveillance system in a study that the paper indicated was "funded by Elbit Systems of America through a contract with the University of Texas at Dallas" without mentioning the amount of financial support. The report also noted that the company had provided "far-field video clips" to help conduct their research on target recognition. The researchers did not respond to requests for comment about the nature of their work and ties to Elbit. Disclosure Gap Section 117 of the generally requires a federally assisted university to report covered gifts and contracts from a foreign source when they meet or exceed $250,000, including multi-year contracts meeting that threshold over their duration. Under the Education Department's example, a five-year research contract worth $50,000 a year is reportable at signing because its lifetime value is $250,000. The Education Department's inspector general in February 2025 that oversight of the system was weak with insufficient controls to ensure reporting requirements were being met. The current disclosure thresholds also make it easier for foreign countries to contribute amounts below that number to avoid triggering reporting requirements but can be significant for individual research projects. That lack of oversight contributes to a situation in which millions of dollars from a foreign military under increasing scrutiny in the U.S. for human rights abuses and facing genocide charges from international courts has been able to spend millions of dollars funding military research at American universities. These relationships are now coming under greater scrutiny at a time when public opinion on Israel has soured in the U.S. due to the genocide in Gaza and Israeli conduct in other regional conflicts. "No self-respecting university should accept funding from Israel, given its destabilizing, destructive, and inhumane use of U.S. weapons," said Hartung. _As a mother who 's passionate about youth sports, I felt the urge to intervene._I didn't go for the publicity... I went to stand up for something I'm passionate about and am prepared to staunchly defend.When I first launched this campaign for U.S. Senate in Minnesota, _I knew I would have to prepare myself and my family for the pain and vitriol that would be slung my way._**But, never in my wildest dreams would I imagine something so basic to be the cause of such heated debate. Biology isn 't complicated. Women are born with a specific set of chromosomes. So are men. They're different.

**That's why we have women's divisions in sports, so women can compete on a fair playing field.

And every roster is finite. Every team excludes someone. That's not bigotry, that's how sports work.

| | | Friends, it’s Al Franken.
---
I don’t scare easy. I’ve been booed by a studio audience and confirmed by the U.S. Senate. (In that order!)
But I’ll tell you what _does_ scare me: the idea that House control could come down to a few hundred votes in one Upstate New York congressional district, and that district happens to be NY-19. (I won my first race by 312 votes, so I know this fear can become a reality.)
No pressure, folks.
My former staffer and friend Josh Riley already beat the odds once. He flipped this seat in a district that wasn’t supposed to be winnable, and he’s spent his first term actually fighting for the people who sent him there: taking on greedy corporations and corruption in Washington to lower costs.
So naturally, the MAGA money machine hates him. They’ll spend whatever it takes to beat Josh and turn Upstate New York red.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b9c51fac-5963-47ee-8231-d6a1ad8710c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

On day one as Governor, I would fire Abbott-appointed Texas Education Commissioner Mike Morath and appoint an educator to lead the Texas Education Agency (TEA). As the Commissioner of Education, Mike Morath has been growing his and Greg Abbott's power at the expense of Texas kids. Instead of prioritizing good teachers in the classroom and smaller class size, Morath has doubled the size of the agency he oversees while schools close and teachers stop teaching. That seems backwards to me.
According to a 2024 survey cited in Texas' own Legislative Budget Board [teacher retention report](https://substack.com/redirect/c716444d-0fa6-449c-8e8e-bc05bef5edc3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), 78% of Texas neighborhood school teachers said they had considered leaving their jobs in the previous year. When that same question was asked in 2020, only 58% of teachers had felt that way. That's a huge jump that we should all be concerned about.
The problem isn't just that teachers are _thinking_ about leaving, they are _actually leaving_. In some instances, teachers are leaving the teaching profession altogether (attrition) while other people switch school districts or join a non-teaching role within their same district (turnover). This distinction matters, but both present a challenge: **if we can 't convince teachers to stay in our classrooms, we can't build the experienced teaching workforce Texas kids need.**
In the 2020-21 school year, Texas' teacher turnover rate was 14.3%. By 2022-23, it had jumped to 21.4% before falling to 19.1% the following year. The attrition rate, meanwhile, reached an all-time high of 13.5% in 2022-23.
_So why are teachers leaving?_
The answers really shouldn't surprise any of us: improper compensation and unmanageable workloads.
In one statewide poll, 41% of Texas teachers said they were working multiple jobs because the money they earned as a teacher was not enough to cover their expenses. That's four out of ten teachers who have to clock in somewhere else after spending all day educating and building up the next generation. Additionally, teachers have expressed difficulty managing their workloads. Teachers report not having enough time to plan out curriculum because of other burdensome administrative tasks.
_What 's the solution?_
Pay our teachers competitive salaries! In addition to that, we have to do better at building supportive school environments that allow teachers to thrive. Nearly one-third of Texas' teaching workforce has fewer than five years of experience. These are the teachers most likely to leave which means we don't have a sustainable pipeline. Teachers need years in the classroom to hone their craft, learn what works, mentor the next generation of educators and build relationships with the students, families and communities they serve.
**If we want Texas kids to succeed, we have to give them great teachers. If we want great teachers, we have to give new educators the support and mentorship they need to become great teachers. And once they become great teachers, we have to give them a reason to stay.**
That requires intentional investment on the part of policy makers and legislators. We have to listen to our teachers and take their recommendations on how to improve their working environment and student outcomes seriously.
Change like that starts at the very top. That's why I have made improving education my number one priority in my race for Governor and have every intention of appointing an educator as head of TEA. We need someone who understands our classrooms because they've actually worked in one -- and will always put the needs of our teachers and students first.
-- Gina

Hey Peter,
---
I know it feels like we’ve been talking a lot about “The Big Beautiful Bill” lately, but we have to ... because there’s a lot to unpack that really affects people in District 13. One of the bill's major cuts was to food assistance programs like the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, better known as SNAP. Government programs like SNAP support low-income families and are focused on reducing hunger and malnutrition in the US. The bill cut SNAP funding by more than $200 million, which is leading to an average cut to families across the US of about $234 a month in assistance. The cuts also included eligibility changes and new requirements to qualify for assistance. Representative Brad Knott voted for the Big Beautiful Bill, even though it would leave 1.4 million North Carolina residents, including 600,000 children, at risk of losing food assistance. People in our communities rely on these programs to help make ends meet. SNAP is especially important today with the cost of living continuing to increase. Harnett County has more than 15% of residents relying on SNAP benefits, and Johnston County has more than 12%. Brad Knott continues to vote along party lines to appease party leadership and the President. He doesn't care how his vote affects our neighbors because he isn't listening to us. I’m ready to advocate for our community by supporting legislation that addresses problems our community faces and uplifts our neighbors into better positions to support themselves. That's what a representative should be doing. We have less than 75 days until voting begins across the district, and I need everyone’s help to keep spreading the word about this race. body:
Our campaign has entered a new chapter.
#
[](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260824-jjp.bccD_u&refcode=em20260824-38192&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=38192%2E1203867%2E5SdZa0)
Peter, it’s Justin J. Pearson.
When Tennessee Republicans passed new, unfair, racist maps designed to **_eliminate TN-09_ as the state’s _only majority-Black_ , Democratic district** — they thought that would be the end of our Movement.
**They couldn’t have been more wrong.**
We’re still here. We’re still mobilizing our People and communities. And we’re still building something the far-right can’t buy and can’t take away from us.
**That’s truly powerful, Peter.** But now our campaign has entered a new chapter — one that’s going to test us in different ways than anything we’ve faced so far. As we continue forging ahead to the general election in November, I’m hoping I can count on your support.
**[So please, split a donation of $9 or more between our Movement and Justice Democrats to Defend District 9 and its communities from the GOP’s authoritarian power grab.](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/141148?c0=jd-em-20260824-jjp.LoQRfX&refcode=em20260824-38192&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=38192%2E1203867%2E5SdZa0)**

After the Supreme Court gave the green light, Donald Trump and his extremist allies have been eager to push racist redistricting schemes — across the South, state by state, district by district, so they can choose their voters instead of letting voters choose their leaders.
And Republicans have eagerly backed this effort. _Why?_ It’s simple: **when more People can freely and fairly participate in our democracy, Republicans risk losing their grip on power.**
I won’t sugarcoat it — we have our work cut out for us. The new TN-09 is _vast._ Which means we have more miles to travel, more voters to reach, more noise to cut through, and more pressure from people who want us to run out of steam.
But I’ve seen what this Movement is capable of. With your support, we will emerge victorious and deliver the better tomorrow that our neighbors and communities have been waiting for.
**[Peter, split a donation of $9 or more in the next 9 minutes between Justice Democrats and our grassroots campaign to defend our district from those who have come to do us harm.](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/141148?c0=jd-em-20260824-jjp.LoQRfX&refcode=em20260824-38192&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=5&akid=38192%2E1203867%2E5SdZa0)**

In Love and Service,
Justin J. Pearson

* * *
Hey folks,
This one is a wild ride. Andrew Tate is behind bars, his public campaign for help is getting more desperate, and the political allies he seems to be counting on aren't rushing to save him.
We get into the Tate brothers' attempts to pull Trump and J.D. Vance into the story, the racism argument coming from their lawyer, and the bigger question underneath all of this: how did these guys build an image of wealth, power, and masculinity that captured the attention of so many young men?
* [**00:01:27**] Tate makes his pitch to Trump--and I break down why MAGA doesn't seem interested in coming to his rescue.
* [**00:04:05**] The Tate brothers' lawyer turns to a racism defense, and the contradictions get pretty remarkable.
* [**00:07:05**] Their carefully constructed image of extraordinary wealth starts colliding with what their lawyers are reportedly arguing in court.
* [**00:10:08**] Tate's posts from behind bars get increasingly dramatic as he claims he's being pressured to take a deal.
* [**00:14:13**] We end on the part that matters beyond the Tates: what masculinity actually means and why liberal men need to be part of that conversation.

This isn't just about watching the Tate brothers' public image unravel. It's about the influence they've had on young men, the political movement that entertained them, and what happens when an online persona finally crashes into reality. We can't just mock this stuff--we have to offer something better. **If you value conversations like this, help me keep them going. Like, comment, and share this with someone you know.**

**If Republicans lose Arizona in 2026, we lose control for the next decade.**

body:
Here's what the numbers say about this moment. | | | Peter, let me share a few numbers: **455,000.** That's how many people hold DACA today — and that's how many parents, coworkers, and neighbors are living in limbo as DACA is being chipped away at piece by piece every day. **More than 1.5 million.** That's how many people were eligible for DACA but have never been able to apply, because courts closed the program to new applicants. That closure was an early move in what has become a deliberate mass delegalization agenda. **Over 250,000.** That's the number of U.S. citizen children with a parent who has DACA. Without protections, hundreds of thousands of American families face permanent separation. **At least 340.** That's how many DACA recipients have been detained under this administration, and more than 90 have been deported. Those are only the cases we know about. **11 million.** That's how many undocumented immigrants we're fighting for. clean_body: Here's what the numbers say about this moment. | | | Peter, let me share a few numbers: 455,000. That's how many people hold DACA today — and that's how many parents, coworkers, and neighbors are living in limbo as DACA is being chipped away at piece by piece every day. More than 1.5 million. That's how many people were eligible for DACA but have never been able to apply, because courts closed the program to new applicants. That closure was an early move in what has become a deliberate mass delegalization agenda. Over 250,000. That's the number of U.S. citizen children with a parent who has DACA. Without protections, hundreds of thousands of American families face permanent separation. At least 340. That's how many DACA recipients have been detained under this administration, and more than 90 have been deported. Those are only the cases we know about. 11 million. That's how many undocumented immigrants we're fighting for. DACA was never enough — it left over 10 million people behind. $10. That's the contribution we're asking for today, so we can keep organizing towards a better future for all working people. If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | | | | | | | | Immigrant youth have won in the past — and with your help, we’ll do it again. — Nico, United We Dream Follow us on: | | | | |

Kristina Knickerbocker is exactly the kind of fearless, people-powered leader we were built to back.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260824-1&t=1&akid=3915%2E587540%2EXmZAvJ)
Exciting news, Peter:
**Leaders We Deserve is proud to announce we’re endorsing Kristina Knickerbocker for Congress in Ohio’s 10th Congressional District!**
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260824_1_knickerbocker.X2vfKH&refcode=em20260824-3915&t=2&akid=3915%2E587540%2EXmZAvJ)
I’ll tell you more about Kristina, but first, this is a critical red-to-blue race that we need to win for Ohio. **[Will you split a $5 contribution between Kristina and Leaders We Deserve today to help us flip this seat?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260824_1_knickerbocker.X2vfKH&refcode=em20260824-3915&amount=5&t=3&akid=3915%2E587540%2EXmZAvJ)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260824_1_knickerbocker.X2vfKH&amount=5&refcode=em20260824-3915&t=4&akid=3915%2E587540%2EXmZAvJ)**
**Kristina Knickerbocker has spent her life serving others.** First as an Air Force major, where she led medical teams and improved care for active duty service members and their families, and then as a neuro-oncology nurse practitioner at Ohio State University Medical Center, where she watched our broken, for-profit healthcare system force cancer patients to choose between life saving treatment and groceries.
She knows this fight personally, and deeply. She has lived the harrowing experiences working people face, both as a patient and as a provider, and it’s made her more determined to fight for a healthcare system that actually works for patients, not insurance companies.
In Congress, Kristina will fight to restore ACA subsidies so working families can actually afford coverage, pass paid family leave so no parent has to choose between their job and their newborn, and take on the maternal mortality crisis that nearly took her own life. She’ll fight to overturn Citizens United and get big money out of politics, and demand real ethics reform for a Supreme Court that has spent years operating without meaningful oversight.
Her opponent, Mike Turner, has been in Congress for over 20 years, taking millions in corporate PAC money. He voted to slash food assistance for hundreds of thousands of Ohioans, and gutted Medicaid coverage for nearly 200,000 working people in his own state. And he eliminated the energy tax credits that were creating Ohio jobs and keeping utilities prices down — _all to protect breaks for billionaires._
**Peter, OH-10 is winnable, and Kristina is exactly the candidate to win it.**
She brings something Turner never could: a lifetime of service to her community, and the conviction that comes from having lived the struggles she’s running to fix.
But Kristina can’t win this race without you.
**Leaders We Deserve doesn’t take a single dollar from corporate PACs or special interests — and neither does Kristina.** Our ability to back candidates like her depends entirely on grassroots supporters like you showing up when it counts. And right now is exactly when your support makes the biggest difference.
**[So Peter, will you split a $5 contribution between Kristina Knickerbocker and Leaders We Deserve today to help us flip OH-10 from red to blue?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260824_1_knickerbocker.X2vfKH&refcode=em20260824-3915&amount=5&t=5&akid=3915%2E587540%2EXmZAvJ)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

So he sent his most loyal puppet to Maine to try and squash our chances. Trump and Vance are trying to erase nearly 30 years of Susan Collins’ failures with one trip to Maine. Mainers are a hell of a lot smarter than that. Susan Collins confirmed key justices who overturned Roe v. Wade. She greenlit cuts to Medicare and Medicaid that threaten rural hospitals. She has fallen in line with Trump 96% of the time. Now, she is hoping that JD Vance, of all people, can distract Mainers from her horrible record. Susan Collins is hoping her party and $60 million in outside support can save her. # **First deportation flight to Haiti since TPS termination includes gang members, sex offenders**
DHS deported **[162 Haitian nationals on the first flight to Haiti](https://substack.com/redirect/e67c7ea7-1421-45aa-960b-c6d3947d7033?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** since the Trump administration ended Temporary Protected Status for roughly 350,000 Haitians, following a June Supreme Court ruling allowing the termination. Officials released details on 15 deportees with convictions including sexual crimes against minors, assault, and gang affiliations with groups like Zoe Pound and 88 Crush Mob.

# **Trump ramps up "economic D-Day" pressure campaign against Iran**
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is set to **[announce new secondary sanctions](https://substack.com/redirect/13010d16-a3ea-4695-a919-de345fdc3353?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Monday targeting nations and entities propping up Iran's economy, part of an intensified campaign as the U.S.-Iran conflict approaches six months, aimed at pushing Tehran toward capitulation or negotiations.

subject: I refuse to be silent in the face of Islamophobia
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
I stood up for Muslim Americans — and Nancy Mace doubled down on her anti-Muslim rhetoric. I’m not backing down.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260824-6637-footer&t=1&akid=6637%2E420207%2E5d5_yR)
I'm furious, Peter.
Nancy Mace just declared herself a “total Islamophobe” because I had the nerve to stand up for Muslim Americans and call out her hateful rhetoric.
[](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260824.jNOadk&refcode=em20260824-6637&t=2&akid=6637%2E420207%2E5d5_yR)
I’ve seen this kind of anti-Muslim rhetoric before. I’ve lived it time and time again.
I came to this country from India when I was just 16 years old. And after 9/11, I watched many people’s fear and grief turn into something ugly — hatred directed at Muslim Americans and immigrant communities across the country.
People I knew. People I cared about. People who had done nothing wrong, they simply existed as exactly who they are.
That’s when I became an organizer — and it’s why I’ve fought for immigrants’ rights and dignity my entire career.
Let me be clear, Peter. **Hatred and bigotry have no place in our country, much less in our government.** I refuse to stay silent while a sitting member of Congress uses her platform to dehumanize Muslim Americans and call it patriotism.
To Muslim Americans across this country: I meant every word I said, and I’ll keep saying it for as long as I need to. Your presence is not a threat, and you belong here. In our government, and in every corner of America.
[**This fight is personal to me — the people this administration and its allies keep targeting need fierce defenders. If you’re able, will you pitch in $3 to help me keep standing up in Congress?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260824.jNOadk&refcode=em20260824-6637&amount=3&t=3&akid=6637%2E420207%2E5d5_yR)

Pramila Jayapal

| | | I just got back from Ukraine.
I’m one of a small handful of Members of Congress to travel there in the past year — and I need to tell you what I saw, and why it matters so much to this fight.
For over four years, Ukraine has been fighting for its survival against Vladimir Putin's unprovoked invasion. I've stood with them since day one. I've led bipartisan legislation to arm Ukraine's military. I've fought to hold Russia accountable for war crimes. I've warned, again and again, that appeasing Putin doesn't bring peace — it invites the next invasion.
**Here's what I saw on this trip: A country still fighting, still resilient, still holding the line — and increasingly uncertain about whether America is still standing 100% behind them.**
That uncertainty didn't come from nowhere. Donald Trump has spent his presidency squeezing Ukraine while handing Vladimir Putin exactly what he wants. **I didn't take this trip for a photo opportunity. I took it because Ukraine needs to know that not every American leader has abandoned them — and because I wanted to see, firsthand, what's actually at stake in Ukraine.**
This is exactly why Equal Opportunity Now exists. We need Democrats in office who understand that standing up to authoritarian aggression isn't optional — it's central to who we are as a country. MAGA Republicans cannot be trusted with this. Time and again, they have shown they'll trade away our allies' security for a photo op with a dictator.

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: So what did DOGE accomplish?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
Trump will always put himself first. Always.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2999%2E4032634%2ExvbMH-)
---
DOGE quietly deleted itself over the summer — saying its mission had come to an end. Here’s the kicker: Elon Musk’s pet project that promised to cut trillions in “waste” actually put our government in EVEN MORE debt. Did DOGE make our government work better? No. It pushed out 300,000 federal workers and now agencies are struggling to try to hire them back. Did DOGE cut waste? Nope. A Senate investigation found out that DOGE generated $21.7 billion in waste in six months alone. So what DID DOGE accomplish? It let Elon Musk dodge more than $2 billion in liabilities while his company sat under federal investigation. It gutted the IRS, risking losing hundreds of billions of dollars in taxes that wealthy tax cheats may never pay. It tried to weaponize social security — a whistleblower said DOGE planned to mark 2.7 million living people as dead to force immigrants out of the country. While he was operating under the veil of “rooting out waste” in our government, Musk was cutting funding for cancer research, veterans programs, and aid for American farmers, all while making $8 million a day from government contracts. He got to act as co-President of the United States, sitting in the Oval Office, joining Cabinet meetings, and making official decisions, all while making $8 million a day on government contracts while he’s at it. He cruelly halted humanitarian aid efforts in real-time — costing lives. And he and his band of weird 22-year-old programmers were gaining access to the private financial information of millions of Americans. Look, I agree that the federal government can waste a lot of money. I’ve spent years trying to squeeze that waste out of the budget: Going after defense contractors who overcharge taxpayers, going after insurers gaming Medicare for billions of dollars, and going after billionaire tax cheats who dodge the taxes that everybody else pays. But DOGE was never about cutting waste. Instead it served the interests of the rich and the powerful and it left the American people far worse off. Elon Musk, Trump, and this administration need to be held accountable. They lied. They took a chainsaw to lifesaving programs that taxpayers paid for. They think they can just get away with it. But I’m going to stay on this. Elizabeth

| | **I am proud to have earned the support of two organizations committed to protecting our environment: Sierra Club's Washington chapter and SEEC PAC, the political arm of the Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition.** **[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137849310/642149186/1596212816?refcode=2026-08-24-environment&recurring=&amount=7&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=5e5c5582-11a0-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ZTVjNTU4Mi0xMWEwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=gIs9DrutxfWwdVEtPY5g_dq5TPO5kJfLaHc31tnCoeY=)** Their support means a great deal because protecting Northwest Washington's environment is about more than preserving the places we love. It is about protecting our way of life and strengthening our local economy. **The Sierra Club's slogan is "Enjoy, explore, and protect the planet." I cannot imagine a better place in the county to do just that than Northwest Washington.** From rolling hills, stunning valleys, and beautiful landscapes along the Puget Sound and the Salish Sea to our diverse ecosystem that supports large migrations of shorebirds, beloved salmon returns, and the iconic bald eagle. Northwest Washington is beloved by environmentalists and adventurers alike. **Beyond the stunning scenery, our landscapes and natural resources are a key component of our local economy.** The rivers throughout the district have deposited rich soils that contribute to some of the finest agricultural land in the country.**Northwest Washington's fertile soil must be cared for and protected.** Further, our district's proximity to the Pacific Ocean makes our coastal communities major economic centers, and **we have a responsibility to protect ocean habitats and scenic shorelines through thoughtful policy-making and clean energy innovation.** **In Congress, I have made mitigating climate change a top priority:**
* I helped draft and pass the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, which continues to invest federal dollars into green jobs, provides Washingtonians with more transportation options, eases congestion in local communities, and reduces carbon pollution across the state;
* My bill to reauthorize the Northwest Straits Commission passed the House. The Commission is a community-led effort to restore marine habitats in the Northwest Straits region and address local threats to marine environments;
* My Water Resources Development Act of 2026 passed out of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee with unanimous bipartisan support. The bill protects Northwest Washington's environment, supports Columbia River Treaty negotiations, and authorizes critical investments in Northwest Washington.

Washington is a beautiful state, and it is a privilege to work with Sierra Club's Washington chapter and SEEC PAC to mitigate climate change and protect our home. clean_body: I have earned the endorsements of Sierra Club’s Washington chapter and SEEC PAC! | | | | I am proud to have earned the support of two organizations committed to protecting our environment: Sierra Club's Washington chapter and SEEC PAC, the political arm of the Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition. = Their support means a great deal because protecting Northwest Washington's environment is about more than preserving the places we love. It is about protecting our way of life and strengthening our local economy. The Sierra Club's slogan is "Enjoy, explore, and protect the planet." I cannot imagine a better place in the county to do just that than Northwest Washington. From rolling hills, stunning valleys, and beautiful landscapes along the Puget Sound and the Salish Sea to our diverse ecosystem that supports large migrations of shorebirds, beloved salmon returns, and the iconic bald eagle. Northwest Washington is beloved by environmentalists and adventurers alike. Beyond the stunning scenery, our landscapes and natural resources are a key component of our local economy. The rivers throughout the district have deposited rich soils that contribute to some of the finest agricultural land in the country.Northwest Washington's fertile soil must be cared for and protected. Further, our district's proximity to the Pacific Ocean makes our coastal communities major economic centers, and we have a responsibility to protect ocean habitats and scenic shorelines through thoughtful policy-making and clean energy innovation. In Congress, I have made mitigating climate change a top priority: I helped draft and pass the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, which continues to invest federal dollars into green jobs, provides Washingtonians with more transportation options, eases congestion in local communities, and reduces carbon pollution across the state; My bill to reauthorize the Northwest Straits Commission passed the House. The Commission is a community-led effort to restore marine habitats in the Northwest Straits region and address local threats to marine environments; My Water Resources Development Act of 2026 passed out of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee with unanimous bipartisan support. The bill protects Northwest Washington's environment, supports Columbia River Treaty negotiations, and authorizes critical investments in Northwest Washington. Washington is a beautiful state, and it is a privilege to work with Sierra Club's Washington chapter and SEEC PAC to mitigate climate change and protect our home. name: Scott Wiener
subject: My first bill crossed the line last week
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Scott WIENER FOR CONGRESS
body:
| |
Peter - August 31st is the last day the Legislature can pass a bill this year - it’s also _my last day in the State Senate._

Nine of my bills are on the floor:

The No Kings Act.
Plug-in solar.
Enforcement teeth for the mask ban.
Heat pumps.
A research bond for a state whose federal science funding is being dismantled.
Medi-Cal coverage.
More civil rights protections.

**I didn’t inherit these fights - I brought them.

I wrote these bills. Just as I wrote landmark laws to pave the way for millions of homes.**

And the $35 insulin cap, in effect since January;
and the $1.1 billion that kept BART and Muni alive;
and the nation’s first corporate carbon disclosure law;
and the nation’s first ban on masked ICE agents.

That’s my record - I’m so proud of this work. And I’m so grateful for your support.

**But here’s the part that keeps me up at night now: None of it continues on its own.**

On September 1, I have just 64 days to fight for a seat in Congress so I can take this work to a national stage.

**If I win, every one of these fights goes to Washington with me - but if I lose...**

Political insiders and special interests have picked their side in this race and they are spending huge amounts of money and pulling every string they have for their candidate.

I don’t need them. **I have you, Peter.** [Will you support my campaign at this crucial moment so we can build momentum as my time in the Senate ends? name: Deb Haaland
subject: I rock my ribbon skirt to honor my ancestors
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/134?t=1&akid=11881%2E400544%2EAG4AfR)
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15614?refcode=jtk1250-fr-nd&t=2&akid=11881%2E400544%2EAG4AfR)
Hi friend, it's Deb Haaland. I am the daughter of Pueblo women, a single mother, a former small business owner, a former Congresswoman, and the first Native American Cabinet Secretary in U.S. history. **And thanks to your support, I am the official Democratic nominee for Governor of New Mexico.**
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15614?refcode=jtk1250-fr-nd&t=3&akid=11881%2E400544%2EAG4AfR)
---
But no matter where I go and no matter what role I serve in, **I'm a proud Pueblo woman.** That's why I often wear my mocs or my ribbon skirt. These symbols remind me of how powerful traditional clothing is in sharing our heritage, and they remind me to honor the shoulders I stand on.

In a minute, I'm going to share some of the places I've rocked my ribbon skirt and mocs. [ _**But before I do, I have to ask:**_**_Will you please help fuel our fight to the general election by giving $5 to my campaign right now?_**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16200?refcode=jtk1250-fr-nd&t=4&akid=11881%2E400544%2EAG4AfR)
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15614?refcode=jtk1250-fr-nd&t=5&akid=11881%2E400544%2EAG4AfR)
---
| | On the day I was sworn in as Secretary of the Interior, I decided to wear my white moccasins and a handmade ribbon skirt adorned with butterflies, stars, and corn. No matter where I go, I am a proud Pueblo woman first — including at the Department of the Interior.
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/8175?refcode=jtk1250-fr-nd&t=6&akid=11881%2E400544%2EAG4AfR)
---
| | On the first day of the White House Tribal Nations Summit in 2021, I wore my beaded moccasins in solidarity with our Indigenous people across the country. I am incredibly grateful that together, our administration made extraordinary accomplishments for Indian Country — enduring progress that would make our ancestors proud.
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15614?refcode=jtk1250-fr-nd&t=7&akid=11881%2E400544%2EAG4AfR)
---
| | From my ancestral homelands here in New Mexico to the halls of Congress — and as I filed my candidate petition to add my name to New Mexico's ballot for Governor — I rock my ribbon skirt to honor my ancestors.
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15614?refcode=jtk1250-fr-nd&t=8&akid=11881%2E400544%2EAG4AfR)
---
Friend, history has shown us there’s nothing we can’t accomplish when we work together, which is why I’m counting on the support of people like you as we fight for a New Mexico that works for everyone.
This race is heating up, friend, and I need your help. **I am ready to fight for an education that gives every child the chance to dream big and reach their full potential here in New Mexico. Give families a raise by increasing the minimum wage and the child tax credit. Protect affordable healthcare for all New Mexicans who depend on it. And with less than three months to go until Election Day, we are one step closer to making this vision a reality.
**
**_[Please, friend: Will you chip in $5 right now so we can build a strong campaign capable of winning this race and making history again?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16200?refcode=jtk1250-fr-nd&t=9&akid=11881%2E400544%2EAG4AfR)_**
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15614?refcode=jtk1250-fr-nd&t=10&akid=11881%2E400544%2EAG4AfR)
---
I am so grateful for your support. Thank you for being by my side.

Be fierce,
Deb
